factors.description: Whether the inspection fell inside the vehicle's day and km interval since the previous inspection.

factors.name: recheck_booked
factors.description: Mitigation: a dated recheck slot or a reserved replacement tyre or pad set is logged for advisory items.

factors.name: pressure_deviation_pct
factors.description: Largest deviation of a recorded cold pressure from the axle specification in the vehicle record.

factors.name: tyre_age_years
factors.description: Age of the oldest fitted tyre, derived from its date code against the inspection date. Steer tyres over 10 years are not permitted.

sections.name: vehicle
sections.description: Fleet number, registration, model, axle layout, tyre size and pressure spec, inspection interval, recorded odometer.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Inspection id, date, depot bay, inspector id, odometer, sign-off timestamp.

sections.name: brakes
sections.description: Per-axle pad or lining thickness, disc state, roller test efficiencies (service, secondary, parking).

sections.name: tyres
sections.description: List by wheel position: serial, date code, min tread mm, cold pressure kPa, retread flag.

sections.name: defects
sections.description: Carried and new defect list: id, raised date, component, category, status, rectified date, technician id.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Previous inspection date and odometer, tyre fitment register by position, booked recheck slots and reserved parts.

F221.rendering_notes: worst_tread_margin_mm appears only as tyres[].min_tread_mm, which is the margin plus 1.0. The legal and advisory limits are never printed, and other positions get plausible higher values. worst_lining_margin_mm appears as brakes.axles[].lining_mm, which is the margin plus 3.0. service_brake_efficiency_pct appears as brakes.test.service_pct. secondary_pct and parking_pct are always comfortably passing decoys. When missing_element is brake_test_null, brakes.test is null, and rectify_urgency then rests on the measured items. tyre_serial_mismatch is shown by comparing tyres[].serial and position against history.fitment_register[]. A transposition swaps two positions' serials. An unregistered serial is absent from the register. A removed tyre is marked removed_date in the register yet still appears on the sheet. odometer_conflict is a difference between inspection.odometer_km and vehicle.odometer_km, or inspection.odometer_km below history.prev_odometer_km. tyre_position_missing drops one expected position given vehicle.axle_config, e.g. 5 entries for a 6-wheel layout. inspector_signoff_null sets inspection.signoff_at and inspector_id to null. carried_defects_open appears as defects[] entries with carried true, status open and rectified_date null. rectification_unverified gives a closed carried defect a rectified_date earlier than raised_date or a null technician_id. interval_status must be computed from inspection.date minus history.prev_date against vehicle.interval_days, and the odometer gap against vehicle.interval_km. on_boundary lands exactly on, or within 1 of, a limit. recheck_booked appears as history.rechecks[] with a future date, or history.reserved_parts[] matching the advisory component. pressure_deviation_pct is shown by comparing tyres[].pressure_kpa with vehicle.tyre_spec front and rear kPa. tyre_age_years is derived from tyres[].date_code (week and year) against inspection.date. Decoys: tyre brand differences, retread flags on rear positions, body or interior defects in defects[] with category cosmetic, new minor defects already closed same day, bay number and inspector grade. No record may contain fields such as fit_for_service, urgency, risk, pass/fail summaries, overdue flags, mismatch flags or computed margins. Every answer must be inferred by comparing values across sections.

F222.role: Research ethics screening officer at a university research ethics office, checking each incoming application before it is allocated to reviewers
F222.setting: Applications for research involving human participants reach the ethics office as structured records assembled from the online submission form, uploaded consent materials and the office's attachment tracker. The screening officer reviews one application at a time. For each one they compare the protocol against the consent materials and data management plan, check required attachments and history, gauge residual participant risk and time pressure, and decide how the application proceeds. Applications range from anonymous staff surveys to clinical-adjacent studies with vulnerable groups. The office has no free-text notes in the screening view, only structured fields.

procedures_disclosed.instructions: Every procedure in the protocol is described in the participant information sheet.

retention_within_consent.instructions: Planned data retention and storage stay within what participants consented to.

criteria.true: Duration and location within consent terms, or approved exception filed.
criteria.false: Retention or storage exceeds consent terms with no exception filed.

screening_disposition.instructions: Which screening disposition should this application receive now?

criteria.accept_for_review: Nothing outstanding; forward to reviewers unchanged.
criteria.minor_query: No blocking items; one non-blocking discrepancy flagged while forwarding.
criteria.hold_confirmation: Exactly one blocking item awaits confirmation before forwarding.
criteria.return_revision: Two or more blocking items, or a required section missing.
criteria.decline_ineligible: Data collection already began before approval; cannot be screened.

screening_urgency.instructions: How urgent is screening, judged by days until recruitment starts?
criteria: Recruitment begins more than 60 days after screening
Recruitment begins 31 to 60 days after screening
Recruitment begins 8 to 30 days after screening
Recruitment begins within 7 days or date passed

residual_risk.instructions: What residual risk do the study procedures pose to participants?
criteria: Minimal: no risk elements listed in protocol or participants
Low: risk elements present, each has a documented safeguard
Moderate: exactly one non-invasive risk element lacks a safeguard
High: two or more unsafeguarded elements, none invasive or deceptive
Critical: an invasive or deceptive procedure lacks a safeguard

factors.name: procedure_sheet_mismatch
factors.description: How the protocol procedure list compares with procedures_described in the consent materials: identical, a trivial naming difference for the same procedure, one procedure absent from the sheet, or several absent

factors.name: retention_conflict
factors.description: Whether data_management retention or storage departs from what consent_materials states: none, retention longer than consented, or storage location not named in consent

factors.name: retention_exception_filed
factors.description: Whether an approved data-retention exception reference exists and matches an attachment with status approved; mitigates a retention conflict

factors.name: risk_element_count
factors.description: Number of risk elements in the study (identifiable data, sensitive topic, vulnerable group, physical measurement, deception), spread across protocol and participants sections

factors.name: unsafeguarded_count
factors.description: How many of the non-invasive risk elements have no safeguard_ref or a safeguard_ref pointing to a missing or unapproved attachment; capped at risk_element_count

factors.name: invasive_or_deceptive
factors.description: Whether the protocol includes an invasive procedure (blood sample, biopsy, drug administration) or deception with debrief

factors.name: invasive_safeguard_present
factors.description: Whether the invasive or deceptive procedure has a documented safeguard (clinician present, debrief protocol attached and approved); about half of alarming procedures carry it

factors.name: days_to_start
factors.description: Days between screening date and planned recruitment start in participants section; negative means the date has passed

factors.name: start_date_conflict
factors.description: Whether the recruitment start in participants differs from the planned start in application: none, a shift staying within the same urgency band, or a shift crossing a band boundary

factors.name: attachment_blockers
factors.description: Count of required attachments that are missing, unsigned or expired (supervisor declaration, sponsor letter, ethics training certificate, gatekeeper permission)

factors.name: blocker_confirmed_elsewhere
factors.description: Whether an apparently missing or expired attachment is superseded by a later history event (renewed certificate logged, letter received) so it no longer blocks

factors.name: section_missing
factors.description: Whether one required top-level section (consent_materials or data_management) is absent or null

factors.name: collection_started
factors.description: Whether history shows data collection events dated before screening, indicating the study began without approval; a pilot under a separate approved reference is the benign look-alike

factors.name: decoy_noise
factors.description: Alarming-looking but irrelevant fields: high prior resubmission count, international collaborator flag, large sample size, student applicant

sections.name: application
sections.description: Reference, application type, applicant role, department, submitted_on, screened_on, planned_start, prior_submissions, collaborator flags

sections.name: protocol
sections.description: Design, list of procedures with codes, and risk_elements each with type and safeguard_ref

sections.name: participants
sections.description: Participant groups with age ranges, vulnerability flags, target_n, recruitment_start and recruitment route

sections.name: consent_materials
sections.description: PIS and consent form versions, procedures_described list, retention_stated_months, storage_stated, withdrawal terms

sections.name: data_management
sections.description: Identifiable flag, retention_months, storage_location, exception_ref, anonymisation_point

sections.name: attachments_history
sections.description: Attachments list with code, status, signed and expires_on; dated history events such as received, renewed, data_collected

F222.rendering_notes: No free-text fields; all values structured. procedure_sheet_mismatch: protocol.procedures is a list of {code, name}; consent_materials.procedures_described is a list of names. trivial_naming uses a synonym of the same procedure (e.g. 'semi-structured interview' vs 'interview, semi-structured'; 'saliva swab' vs 'buccal swab'); one_missing or several_missing drop names from the sheet. Lists are reordered so mismatches sit at varied positions. retention_conflict: data_management.retention_months exceeds consent_materials.retention_stated_months, or data_management.storage_location (e.g. 'external_cloud_eu') is not the consent storage_stated value (e.g. 'university_server'). retention_exception_filed: data_management.exception_ref is non-null and matches an attachments_history entry with code DRX and status 'approved'; a decoy variant has exception_ref set but the attachment status 'pending' or a different reference, which does not mitigate. risk_element_count: protocol.risk_elements list entries plus participants.groups vulnerability flags (under_18, lacks_capacity, patients, prisoners); data_management.identifiable true counts as an element. unsafeguarded_count: elements whose safeguard_ref is null or points to an attachment that is missing or not approved. invasive_or_deceptive appears as a procedure code (BLD, BIO, IMP, DEC) in protocol; invasive_safeguard_present as a safeguard_ref to an approved attachment (CLN or DBF). days_to_start: computed from application.screened_on and participants.recruitment_start, never stated as a number. start_date_conflict: application.planned_start differs from participants.recruitment_start; crosses_band places the two dates in different urgency bands so judges may split, and boundary values (exactly 30, 31, 60, 61, 7 or 8 days) are deliberately frequent. attachment_blockers: attachments with status 'missing', signed false, or expires_on before screened_on. blocker_confirmed_elsewhere: a later history event (e.g. 'training_renewed', 'sponsor_letter_received') dated on or before screened_on cancels one blocker. Blocking items for disposition are unresolved attachment blockers, procedures missing from the sheet, and unexcused retention conflicts; trivial naming differences and within-band date shifts are non-blocking. section_missing: consent_materials or data_management is null. collection_started 'yes': a history event 'data_collected' dated before screened_on with no approval reference; 'pilot_under_other_approval' shows the same event carrying an approval_ref to a different approved study, which is benign. decline_ineligible takes precedence over other dispositions. Decoys: application.prior_submissions of 3 or more, intl_collaborator true, target_n in the thousands, applicant_role 'pgr_student'; none affect any answer. The record never contains fields such as risk_tier, urgency, disposition, complete or consistent, and never summarises mismatch counts.

F223.role: Allotment site officer for a borough allotments service, reviewing one plot inspection record at a time to decide tenancy enforcement steps
F223.setting: A municipal allotments team inspects let plots several times a year against a tenancy cultivation standard: at least 75% of bed area under cultivation. Officers review each inspection record alongside the tenancy file, prior notices, hazards found and any messages from the tenant. They decide whether the plot is in breach, whether the formal warning steps allow a notice to quit, what to do next, and how much of the plot is uncultivated. Approved medical exemptions and a 180-day new-tenancy grace period excuse a cultivation shortfall. In the dormant season (November to February), beds under sheet or mulch count as cultivated; in the growing season they do not.

cultivation_breach.instructions: Plot is below the cultivation standard without a valid exemption.

criteria.true: Shortfall confirmed; no approved exemption or grace period applies
criteria.false: Standard met, shortfall excused, or evidence incomplete

notice_ladder_met.instructions: Warning steps are complete, so a notice to quit is now permitted.

criteria.true: Warning served, deadline passed, re-inspected after deadline
criteria.false: A warning step missing, still open, or dated out of order

next_action.instructions: What should the officer do next with this tenancy?

criteria.no_action: Plot meets standard or shortfall excused, and no unmitigated hazard
criteria.hold_recheck: A deciding fact is unconfirmed; book a dated recheck first
criteria.warning_notice: Confirmed unexcused breach or hazard, warning steps not yet complete
criteria.final_notice: Breach persists after a properly served and expired warning

recurrence_count.instructions: How often has this same issue been logged in 12 months?
criteria: First occurrence; not logged in prior 12 months
Logged once before within the past 12 months
Logged two to four times in 12 months
Logged five or more times in 12 months

uncultivated_extent.instructions: What share of the plot's bed area is uncultivated this visit?
criteria: Under 25% of bed area uncultivated
25% to under 50% of bed area uncultivated
50% to under 75% of bed area uncultivated
75% or more of bed area uncultivated

factors.name: cultivated_share
factors.description: True share of bed area under cultivation at this visit. It is never printed as a percentage and must be computed from the beds list (area_m2 and state).

factors.name: inspection_season
factors.description: Whether the visit falls in the growing season (March to October) or the dormant season (November to February). This decides whether covered beds count as cultivated.

factors.name: covered_bed_count
factors.description: Number of beds under sheet, mulch or green manure. These count as cultivated only in the dormant season, so a value near the 75% line can flip the breach.

factors.name: exemption_state
factors.description: Status of any excuse for a shortfall. An approved exemption or a tenancy under 180 days old excuses the shortfall. A pending exemption needs confirmation. An expired one looks like approval but no longer applies.

factors.name: warning_ladder
factors.description: State of prior formal warnings about cultivation. Only a warning that was served and whose deadline has passed supports a notice to quit. A warning logged without a service date does not count.

factors.name: reinspection_out_of_order
factors.description: The follow-up re-inspection is dated before the warning deadline, or before the service date, which invalidates the ladder even when a warning exists.

factors.name: hazard_type
factors.description: Any hazard found on the plot. An unmitigated hazard alone justifies a warning, even when cultivation is fine.

factors.name: hazard_mitigated
factors.description: Whether a found hazard is already being handled. Examples: a removal booked with a date, a structure approved by the site committee, or waste staged for a scheduled site skip day.

factors.name: photo_evidence_missing
factors.description: The inspection photo set is null or empty, so the bed states cannot be verified for an enforcement step.

factors.name: tenant_reply
factors.description: The tenant's latest message. Possible replies: an offered improvement plan, a dispute of the findings, or a claim of illness with no exemption filed. The illness claim makes an excuse merely possible, not established.

factors.name: prior_visit_cultivated_share
factors.description: Cultivated share at the previous visit, shown in history. This is a trend decoy: an improving trend does not excuse a current shortfall.

factors.name: rent_arrears_gbp
factors.description: Outstanding plot rent. This is a decoy that alarms readers but does not bear on the cultivation breach, the warning ladder or the uncultivated extent.

sections.name: tenancy
sections.description: Plot id, site, plot size, start date, rent status and an exemption object, with type, status and dates

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Visit date, officer initials, photos list or null, previous visit summary, and a short officer_note

sections.name: beds
sections.description: List of beds with bed_id, area_m2 and state (cultivated, covered, weedy, bare, overgrown)

sections.name: hazards
sections.description: List of hazards found, each with type, location, action_booked date or null, and committee_approval flag

sections.name: notices
sections.description: List of prior notices with kind, issued_on, served_on or null, deadline, and reinspected_on

sections.name: correspondence
sections.description: One to three one-sentence messages from the tenant or the office, each dated

F223.rendering_notes: cultivated_share is realised only through beds[].area_m2 and beds[].state. The reader sums the areas, and no percentage field ever appears. covered_bed_count sets how many beds have state 'covered'. inspection.visit_date sets inspection_season, and the season is never named. In dormant-season visits, covered beds count as cultivated; in growing-season visits they count as uncultivated. Weedy, bare and overgrown beds are always uncultivated. Place some records within 3 points of the 75% line so the covered beds decide the outcome. exemption_state appears in tenancy.exemption as {type, status, approved_on, expires_on}. medical_pending has status 'requested' and approved_on null. medical_expired has status 'approved' but expires_on before visit_date. This is a decoy. new_tenancy_grace is shown only by tenancy.start_date falling within 180 days of visit_date, with exemption null. warning_ladder appears in notices[]: served_deadline_open has a deadline after visit_date; logged_without_service_date has served_on null. When reinspection_out_of_order is true, reinspected_on falls before the deadline or before served_on. hazard_type fills hazards[]. hazard_mitigated sets action_booked to a future date or committee_approval to true. Otherwise action_booked is null and committee_approval is false. photo_evidence_missing sets inspection.photos to null. In this case the officer_note may still describe the beds confidently, as a decoy. tenant_reply appears as a correspondence message. 'reports_illness_unverified' mentions an illness, but tenancy.exemption stays null or requested. prior_visit_cultivated_share appears as inspection.previous_visit.cultivated_beds out of total beds. rent_arrears_gbp appears as tenancy.rent_status.arrears_gbp. The officer_note should sound alarming or reassuring independently of the true answer. No record may contain fields such as breach, eligible_for_notice, recommended_action, uncultivated_pct or severity, and no message states the decision.

F224.role: Dental radiography clinical audit reviewer, working through individual exposure episodes for a multi-surgery dental group's radiation protection audit
F224.setting: Each record is one radiographic episode from a dental surgery: the referral and justification entries, the logged exposures, the image quality grading, the X-ray unit's QA status and console log, and the operator's audit history. The reviewer reconciles these sections, weighs documented exceptions and equipment context, and decides justification, retake cause, follow-up, dose position and unjustified exposure count. There are no free-text fields; all evidence is in coded values, numbers, dates and flags.

justified.instructions: The exposure was clinically justified by the recorded referral details.

criteria.true: Indication code and recall interval support the requested view
criteria.false: Indication missing, mismatched to view, or interval too short

operator_retake.instructions: The retake was caused by operator technique, not equipment or patient.

criteria.true: Fault codes and equipment checks point to operator technique
criteria.false: No retake, or equipment, patient or unclear cause

follow_up.instructions: What follow-up should the auditor assign to this exposure record?

criteria.close_record: No discrepancies, or all fully explained; audit closes without action.
criteria.log_trend: Trivial unexplained discrepancy; recorded for trend review, no contact.
criteria.hold_confirm: One missing confirmation or sign-off must arrive before closing.
criteria.operator_feedback: Confirmed technique or justification error; operator receives targeted feedback.
criteria.escalate_rpa: Unmitigated dose, equipment or repeated exposure breach referred to adviser.

dose_position.instructions: Where does the verified patient dose sit against the reference level?
criteria: Low: verified dose below 75% of reference level
Typical: verified dose from 75% to 100%
Raised: verified dose above 100%, up to 150%
Excessive: verified dose above 150% of reference level

unjustified_count.instructions: How many logged exposures lack a matching justified request?
criteria: Every logged exposure matches a justified request
Exactly one logged exposure lacks a justified request
Exactly two logged exposures lack justified requests
Three or more logged exposures lack justified requests

factors.name: indication_match
factors.description: How well the referral indication code fits the requested view type (e.g. caries screening code against a bitewing versus a periapical for an unrelated tooth).

factors.name: recall_interval_months
factors.description: Months since the previous radiograph of the same view and region, compared with the minimum interval implied by the recorded caries risk category.

factors.name: dose_ratio_to_drl
factors.description: True ratio of patient dose to the diagnostic reference level for the view; values near 0.75, 1.0 and 1.5 sit on scale boundaries.

factors.name: console_log_discrepancy
factors.description: Disagreement between the exposure list and the unit's console log: none, small time-stamp drift, mismatched kV or exposure time (shifting verified dose), or an extra exposure in the console log absent from the exposure list.

factors.name: retake_cause
factors.description: Underlying cause of any repeat exposure, signalled indirectly by image fault codes, sensor error entries and patient flags.

factors.name: equipment_qa_status
factors.description: State of the X-ray unit's periodic QA at exposure date: in date, overdue, failed last output test, or operating under a logged service visit.

factors.name: approved_exception
factors.description: A documented clinical override (e.g. prescriber-approved shorter recall for symptomatic patient or higher-dose setting for large patient) exists, mitigating interval or dose concerns.

factors.name: patient_cooperation_flag
factors.description: Patient record flags limited cooperation, gag reflex or special care need, offering a benign explanation for movement or positioning faults.

factors.name: unrequested_exposure_count
factors.description: Number of logged exposures that do not correspond to any requested view before mitigation by verbal authorisation.

factors.name: verbal_authorisation_logged
factors.description: A timestamped prescriber authorisation entry covers additional exposures, turning otherwise unrequested exposures into justified ones when its time and view match.

factors.name: image_grade
factors.description: Recorded diagnostic quality grade of the final image after any retake.

factors.name: audit_completeness
factors.description: Whether all audit inputs are present: complete, image grading pending second reviewer, or operator sign-off missing.

factors.name: operator_prior_findings
factors.description: Count of prior confirmed audit findings for the operator in the last 12 months, raising weight of a new technique error.

sections.name: request
sections.description: Referral: requested views, indication code, caries risk category, prescriber id, request date, prior same-view date, exception and verbal authorisation entries.

sections.name: exposures
sections.description: List of logged exposures with view, region, kV, mA, exposure time, recorded dose estimate, timestamp and retake_of reference.

sections.name: image_review
sections.description: Final image grade, fault codes per image, second grader status, sensor error codes.

sections.name: equipment
sections.description: Unit id, last QA date, QA interval, last output test result, service log entries, view reference levels, console log entries.

sections.name: operator
sections.description: Operator id, role, sign-off timestamp or null, prior findings count, last training date.

F224.rendering_notes: indication_match: request.indication_code against request.views_requested; never labelled as matching. recall_interval_months: derived from request.prior_same_view_date versus request.request_date, compared with request.caries_risk (high allows 6 months, moderate 12, low 24). dose_ratio_to_drl: exposures[].dose_est_mGy against equipment.drl_ref[view]; the auditor must compute the ratio, and where console_log_discrepancy is setting_mismatch the console kV/exposure_s imply a different verified dose than the exposure list, so equipment.console_log values govern. console_log_discrepancy: equipment.console_log[] entries compared with exposures[] by timestamp, kV and time; timestamp_drift is under 2 minutes and benign; extra_console_exposure adds an entry with no exposure-list counterpart, which also counts as unjustified. retake_cause: exposures[].retake_of set non-null, with image_review.fault_codes (e.g. FC_APEX_CLIPPED, FC_CONE_CUT, FC_BLUR, FC_OVER_DENSE) and image_review.sensor_errors; sensor_fault shows a sensor error code at the retake timestamp; patient_movement shows FC_BLUR, ambiguous when patient_cooperation_flag is absent. equipment_qa_status: equipment.last_qa_date plus qa_interval_months versus exposure date, equipment.last_output_test (pass/fail), equipment.service_log with open visit window. approved_exception: request.exceptions[] entry with code and approver id, or empty list. patient_cooperation_flag: request.patient_flags list (e.g. GAG_REFLEX, SPECIAL_CARE). unrequested_exposure_count: exposures whose view/region is absent from request.views_requested; verbal_authorisation_logged appears as request.verbal_auth[] with time and view, and only covers exposures with matching view and later timestamp, so sometimes it covers some but not all. image_grade: image_review.final_grade (1/2/3 coded). audit_completeness: image_review.second_grader_status 'pending' or operator.signoff_at null. operator_prior_findings: operator.prior_findings_12m. Decoys: equipment.unit_serial, room id, sensor size, patient age band, operator.last_training_date (usually unrelated), and timestamp_drift entries that look like discrepancies but are harmless. No field may state justification, retake cause attribution, dose percentage, unjustified count or recommended action; no summary, risk or outcome fields. Mismatches are never flagged by the record itself.

F225.domain: waste transfer notes at a recycling centre
F225.role: Weighbridge compliance officer checking incoming waste transfer notes at a municipal recycling centre
F225.setting: Each record is one inbound delivery: the producer's waste transfer note, the carrier's registration details, the weighbridge ticket, the load inspection, the site permit extract and the producer's delivery history. The officer reviews one delivery at a time. They decide whether the declared waste code is borne out by inspection, what to do with the load, what follow-up is needed, how far the weighed quantity departs from the declared one, and how many required note entries are missing.

code_matches_load.instructions: Declared EWC code matches the material recorded at load inspection.

load_disposition.instructions: What should the site do with this load and note?

criteria.accept: Tip normally; documents complete and load matches the note.
criteria.accept_conditional: Tip with downgrade or surcharge; documents complete, load quality short.
criteria.hold: Quarantine load pending one outstanding document or confirmation.
criteria.reject: Turn the load away; it cannot lawfully be received.

follow_up.instructions: What follow-up with the producer or carrier does this note need?

criteria.none: No follow-up; note and load raise no issues.
criteria.file_note: Log a minor discrepancy internally without contacting anyone.
criteria.request_amendment: Ask producer to reissue a corrected transfer note.
criteria.formal_warning: Send written duty-of-care warning to producer or carrier.
criteria.regulator_referral: Refer the note and load to the environmental regulator.

weight_variance.instructions: How far does weighbridge net weight differ from declared quantity?
criteria: Negligible: net within 5% of declared quantity
Minor: net differs by over 5% up to 15%
Major: net differs by over 15% up to 40%
Gross: net differs from declared by over 40%

doc_gaps.instructions: How many required transfer note entries are missing or null?
criteria: All required note entries present and completed
Exactly one required entry missing or null
Two or three required entries missing or null
Four or more required entries missing or null

factors.name: weight_discrepancy_pct
factors.description: Absolute percentage gap between the quantity declared on the note and weighbridge gross minus tare.

factors.name: unit_convention_differs
factors.description: Note declares the quantity in tonnes while the weighbridge reports kg, so the reader must convert before comparing.

factors.name: code_mismatch
factors.description: How the declared EWC code relates to the material observed at inspection.

factors.name: inspection_status
factors.description: Whether the load inspection was carried out and recorded fully.

factors.name: contamination_pct
factors.description: Share of non-target material estimated at inspection; drives downgrade or surcharge.

factors.name: missing_doc_items
factors.description: Number of required note entries left null or absent, drawn from producer_sig, carrier_sig, ewc_code, sic_code, qty, carrier_reg_no, transfer_date and producer_postcode.

factors.name: carrier_reg_state
factors.description: Carrier registration status on the delivery date.

factors.name: renewal_receipt_present
factors.description: A renewal application receipt dated before expiry is on file, mitigating an expired registration.

factors.name: signature_after_delivery
factors.description: The producer signature timestamp falls after the weighbridge time_in, showing the note was completed out of order.

factors.name: moisture_allowance_agreed
factors.description: The contract carries an agreed moisture tolerance covering wet-weather weight gains, mitigating an overweight load.

factors.name: producer_prior_rejections
factors.description: Count of rejected or held loads from this producer in the last 12 months.

factors.name: vehicle_reg_mismatch
factors.description: How the vehicle registration on the note compares with the weighbridge ANPR read.

factors.name: code_on_permit
factors.description: Whether the declared EWC code appears on the site permit's accepted list.

factors.name: boundary_placement
factors.description: Places weight_discrepancy_pct or contamination_pct within 0.5 points of a level threshold, or balances one mitigation against one alarm.

sections.name: transfer_note
sections.description: Producer's note: note_id, transfer_date, producer details, sic_code, ewc_code, qty, qty_unit, container, signatures with timestamps.

sections.name: carrier
sections.description: Carrier name, carrier_reg_no, reg_tier, reg_expiry, renewal_receipt_date, vehicle_reg.

sections.name: weighbridge
sections.description: Ticket_no, time_in, time_out, anpr_reg, gross_kg, tare_kg, tare_source.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Inspected_at, observed_ewc, primary_material, contamination_pct, prohibited_items, photos_count; null if not done.

sections.name: site_permit
sections.description: Permit_ref, accepted_ewc list, daily_cap_t, tonnage_today_t, contract moisture_allowance_pct.

sections.name: producer_history
sections.description: Deliveries_12m, rejections_12m, holds_12m, last_rejection_date, list of recent ticket_nos.

F225.rendering_notes: weight_discrepancy_pct is never stated. It shows only as transfer_note.qty and qty_unit against weighbridge.gross_kg minus tare_kg; when unit_convention_differs, qty is in t and must be converted. moisture_allowance_agreed sets site_permit.moisture_allowance_pct to a value (for example 8) or null. code_mismatch shows as inspection.observed_ewc and primary_material differing from transfer_note.ewc_code; hazardous_mirror_entry uses an asterisked code observed against a non-asterisked declared code. inspection_status not_done sets inspection to null. Partial keeps photos_count but sets observed_ewc and contamination_pct to null, which makes code_matches_load false. missing_doc_items nulls that many required note fields, chosen at random from the listed set. carrier_reg_state shows via carrier.reg_expiry against transfer_date, or carrier_reg_no null or flagged reg_found:false. renewal_receipt_present fills carrier.renewal_receipt_date before reg_expiry. signature_after_delivery makes transfer_note.producer_sig_at later than weighbridge.time_in. vehicle_reg_mismatch alters anpr_reg against carrier.vehicle_reg; transposed_chars is a benign typo. code_on_permit controls whether ewc_code appears in site_permit.accepted_ewc. producer_prior_rejections fills producer_history counts. Decoys: container type, tare_source (stored or fresh), ticket number sequence, tonnage_today_t near but below daily_cap_t, a wet-weather flag in weighbridge without any contract allowance, last_rejection_date older than 12 months, and trivial weight gaps under 1%. Mismatches are never flagged. No field may name an outcome: no variance_pct, missing_count, compliant, risk, status_ok or recommended_action fields. No free-text notes or comments anywhere.

F226.role: Site temporary works inspector reviewing scaffold handover records before the principal contractor accepts each scaffold for use
F226.setting: On a large construction site, scaffold erectors submit a handover record for each completed or altered scaffold. The inspector reads one record at a time, comparing the approved design against the as-built inspection, the defect list, the supporting documents and the free-text notes. They then decide whether the scaffold can be tagged and released, released with limits, held for one confirmation, or refused. Records come from many erection gangs and differ widely in size and type, from small independent tied lifts to multi-bay access scaffolds with loading bays. The erector's proposed tag is frequently optimistic, and erector notes can explain a departure from design without anyone having formally approved it.

design_conformity.instructions: Every departure from design is either absent or covered by approved variation.

criteria.true: No departures, or each lies within an approved variation's scope.
criteria.false: Some departure is unapproved or falls outside variation scope.

handover_decision.instructions: What should be done with this scaffold handover?

criteria.accept_full: Green tag issued; whole scaffold released at design load.
criteria.accept_restricted: Released with written limits on lifts, load or access.
criteria.hold: Not released until one outstanding confirmation is received.
criteria.reject: Refused; erector must complete remedial work before resubmission.

limiting_issue.instructions: Which most severe class of issue does the record show?

criteria.none_found: No open defect, document gap or unapproved design departure.
criteria.paperwork_only: Only documents missing or expired; structure itself recorded sound.
criteria.component_defect: Local missing or damaged parts; design dimensions all met.
criteria.design_departure: Unapproved difference from design in ties, height, lifts or load.

discrepancy_size.instructions: How far does the recorded value differ from the expected value?
criteria: Matches expected value, or differs by under 2%
Differs from expected value by 2% to under 10%
Differs from expected value by 10% to under 25%
Differs from expected value by 25% or more

releasable_share.instructions: What share of the scaffold's lifts can be released for use?
criteria: No lift can be released for use
Fewer than half of the lifts releasable
Half or more releasable, but not every lift
Every lift releasable for its design use

factors.name: lift_height_mismatch
factors.description: Difference between design lifts and maximum height in the design section and the lifts counted and height measured in as_built. Values range from none, through one extra lift, to a height over the maximum with the lift count unchanged (for example, a deeper top lift).

factors.name: tie_shortfall
factors.description: Number of ties fitted in as_built below design.ties_required. Zero means the counts agree. The shortfall is never stated directly and must be worked out by comparing the two counts.

factors.name: load_class_mismatch
factors.description: Agreement between the load class on the design, the load class on the proposed tag in as_built, and the boarding recorded (for example, a heavy-duty class claimed with a single-board platform width).

factors.name: approved_variation
factors.description: Whether design.variation holds an approved temporary works variation (with reference, approver and scope) covering a departure. The scope sometimes covers only part of the actual departure, for example ties on elevation A while the shortfall is on elevation B.

factors.name: open_defect_count
factors.description: Number of entries in the defects list for guardrails, toe boards, boards, brick guards, ladder access or base plates that are not marked closed.

factors.name: rectification_state
factors.description: State of defects that have been raised. Either all are closed and reinspected; some are closed by the erector but not yet reinspected; or the defects remain open.

factors.name: affected_lift_fraction
factors.description: Fraction of lifts carrying an open defect or an unapproved departure. This fraction decides how much of the scaffold can be released, and it must be derived from the lift numbers in the defect entries against the total lifts counted.

factors.name: document_gap
factors.description: A single missing or invalid supporting document: the tie pull test is absent, the design drawing reference on the scaffold section does not match the design section, or the inspector's competence card expired before the inspection date.

factors.name: tie_test_result
factors.description: Result of the tie pull test in docs. A pass dated after the inspection mitigates a small tie shortfall. A fail is serious. The test can also be not done.

factors.name: erector_explanation
factors.description: Whether notes.erector_note gives a benign-sounding reason for a departure, such as ties removed under permit for cladding fixing or a top lift raised at the client's request. The note is not a formal approval and only mitigates when it agrees with a variation entry.

factors.name: alarming_remark_resolved
factors.description: Whether notes.inspector_remark mentions an alarming event (wind gusts overnight, a vehicle strike near the base, a board found split) that the same remark or the defect list shows was checked and cleared.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether the record sits on a threshold. Examples: exactly half of the lifts affected; a tie shortfall of one with the pull test not done; or a variation whose scope wording plausibly but not clearly covers the departure.

factors.name: prior_red_tags
factors.description: Count of earlier red tags on this scaffold ID in the scaffold history. This is a decoy: a history of red tags raises attention but does not decide any question on its own.

sections.name: scaffold
sections.description: Identity and context: scaffold_id, location, drawing_ref, type, bays, prior_red_tags, last_handover date.

sections.name: design
sections.description: Approved design: drawing_ref, rev, design_lifts, max_height_m, ties_required, load_class, and a variation object or null.

sections.name: as_built
sections.description: Inspection findings: inspected_on, inspector, lifts_counted, height_m, ties_fitted, boarding_width_boards, base_condition, tag_proposed.

sections.name: defects
sections.description: List of defect entries: lift, item, raised_on, status, closed_on, reinspected (boolean or null).

sections.name: docs
sections.description: Supporting documents: handover_cert_signed, inspector_card_expiry, and tie_test as an object with date, ties_tested and result, or null.

sections.name: notes
sections.description: Free text: erector_note and inspector_remark, each one or two sentences, either possibly null.

F226.rendering_notes:
How each factor appears in the record:
- lift_height_mismatch: shown only through design.design_lifts and design.max_height_m against as_built.lifts_counted and as_built.height_m.
- tie_shortfall: shown only through design.ties_required against as_built.ties_fitted.
- load_class_mismatch: shown through design.load_class against as_built.tag_proposed.load_class and as_built.boarding_width_boards.
- approved_variation: design.variation is filled in with ref, approved_by and scope text when true, and null when false. When the scope covers only part of the departure, the mismatch is in the scope text (elevation, lift numbers) against where the departure sits.
- open_defect_count and rectification_state: shown through defects[].status, closed_on and reinspected. 'Closed' with reinspected false or null counts as partial.
- affected_lift_fraction: must be derived from defects[].lift and any departure lifts against as_built.lifts_counted.
- document_gap: appears in one of these ways: docs.tie_test is null; scaffold.drawing_ref differs from design.drawing_ref by revision or number; or docs.inspector_card_expiry falls before as_built.inspected_on.
- tie_test_result: docs.tie_test.result is 'pass' or 'fail', or tie_test is null.
- erector_explanation: notes.erector_note text.
- alarming_remark_resolved: notes.inspector_remark text, with resolution stated in the same remark or shown by a closed, reinspected defect.
- boundary_case: values are set exactly on the thresholds.
- prior_red_tags: scaffold.prior_red_tags.

Decoys:
- as_built.tag_proposed is the erector's proposal and is often green when it should not be. It must never be read as the answer.
- prior_red_tags is a decoy.
- The erector_note sounds authoritative but is not an approval.
- Alarming words in inspector_remark are often already resolved.
- Trivial mismatches also appear and should be noticed but not over-weighted, for example a height differing by 0.1 m within rounding.

Rules for decisions:
- The record must never contain fields such as risk, decision, conforms, releasable or severity.
- Hold applies when exactly one confirmation is outstanding: a tie test, reinspection of closed defects, or a corrected drawing reference.
- Accept_restricted applies when physical problems are confined to identifiable lifts.
- Reject applies to an unapproved structural departure or a failed tie test.
- For the limiting_issue question, the most severe class present is the answer.
- The shared discrepancy_size scale applies to the most prominent recorded-versus-expected pair, usually ties fitted against ties required, or height measured against maximum height.
- About half of the records with an alarming departure should carry mitigation (an approved variation, a passing tie test or a resolved remark).
- Some records should have no mismatch at all.

F227.role: Progress review assessor at an apprenticeship training provider, checking one completed quarterly progress review record per apprentice before it is signed off on the provider's system
F227.setting: A training provider delivers apprenticeship standards to apprentices placed with many employers. Every twelve weeks each apprentice has a three-way progress review between the apprentice, the employer mentor and the provider tutor. The review record collects the apprentice's profile, the agreed programme plan, logged progress, attendance and the review meeting details. Before the record is accepted, an assessor reviews it. They work out whether off-the-job hours and knowledge, skills and behaviour (KSB) sign-offs are keeping pace with the plan, and allow for approved breaks or documented absences. They then decide what happens to the record. The record holds structured fields only, with no free-text notes.

gateway_on_track.instructions: The apprentice is on track to reach gateway by planned date.

review_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this progress review record next?

criteria.sign_off: Progress on plan and record complete; accept without actions.
criteria.sign_off_actions: Accept record but set targeted catch-up actions for next period.
criteria.hold_evidence: Withhold sign-off until one missing item or signature arrives.
criteria.support_plan: Open formal support plan with dated recovery targets and checkpoints.
criteria.refer_manager: Refer to programme manager for break or withdrawal decision.

slippage_source.instructions: Which party's shortfall chiefly explains any slippage this period?

criteria.no_slippage: Hours and KSB sign-offs both on plan this period.
criteria.apprentice: Unauthorised missed sessions or evidence not submitted by apprentice.
criteria.employer: Off-the-job time not released or workplace tasks not assigned.
criteria.provider: Sessions cancelled by provider or assessor sign-offs left outstanding.

otj_shortfall.instructions: How far do logged off-the-job hours fall below pro-rata target?
criteria: Met: logged hours at or above pro-rata target
Minor: shortfall under 10% of pro-rata target
Significant: shortfall from 10% to 25% of target
Severe: shortfall above 25% of pro-rata target

ksb_coverage.instructions: What share of KSBs due by now is signed off?
criteria: Under half of due KSBs signed off
Half to under 70% of due KSBs signed off
70% to under 85% of due KSBs signed off
85% to under 100% of due KSBs signed off
Every KSB due by now is signed off

factors.name: otj_shortfall_pct
factors.description: True shortfall of logged off-the-job hours against the pro-rata target after approved breaks are deducted, as a percentage of target; 0 or below means met

factors.name: ksb_signed_share
factors.description: Fraction of KSBs scheduled as due by the review date that appear in the signed-off list

factors.name: mitigation_present
factors.description: Whether an alarming shortfall or absence pattern is accompanied by an approved or documented explanation

factors.name: mitigation_type
factors.description: Form the mitigation takes when present

factors.name: slippage_cause
factors.description: Which party actually caused any slippage, including a mixed case where two parties contribute roughly equally

factors.name: employer_input_missing
factors.description: Employer input section is null and the employer did not attend the review

factors.name: signoff_out_of_order
factors.description: A signature date in the review meeting precedes the meeting date, or the provider signed before the apprentice

factors.name: functional_skills_state
factors.description: English and maths functional skills status needed before gateway

factors.name: weeks_to_gateway
factors.description: Weeks between the review date and the planned gateway date; negative means gateway date already passed

factors.name: prior_reviews_with_actions
factors.description: Count of earlier reviews in history that were signed off with catch-up actions or a support plan

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Shortfall or KSB share placed exactly on or within one unit of a scale threshold, or hours borderline only once pending entries are counted

factors.name: decoy_signal
factors.description: An eye-catching field that does not bear on the decisions

sections.name: apprentice
sections.description: Learner identifiers, standard code and level, start_date, planned_gateway, contracted_hrs_wk, fs_english and fs_maths status objects

sections.name: plan
sections.description: otj_target_total_hrs, planned_weeks, ksbs_due list of codes with due_by dates, breaks list with start, end, approved flag

sections.name: progress
sections.description: otj_logged_hrs, otj_verified_hrs, otj_pending_hrs, ksbs_signed list of code and signed_on date, unit_grades list

sections.name: attendance
sections.description: sessions_scheduled, sessions_attended, sessions_cancelled_by_provider, absences list with date, reason_code, authorised, cert_ref

sections.name: review_meeting
sections.description: review_date, employer_attended, signatures object with apprentice, mentor, tutor dates, prior_reviews list with date and outcome_code

sections.name: employer_input
sections.description: mentor_id, mentor_changed_on, otj_hrs_released, workplace_tasks_assigned, shutdown_from, shutdown_to; null when employer absent

F227.rendering_notes:
Never state a pace, risk, shortfall percentage, on-track flag or recommended outcome. The assessor must derive them.

Off-the-job shortfall (otj_shortfall_pct): render it indirectly. The record gives plan.otj_target_total_hrs and plan.planned_weeks. The weeks elapsed follow from apprentice.start_date to review_meeting.review_date. The pro-rata target is the total target multiplied by elapsed weeks less approved break weeks, divided by planned weeks. Set progress.otj_logged_hrs so the derived shortfall matches the factor. Unapproved breaks appear in plan.breaks with approved:false and must not reduce the target.

KSB share (ksb_signed_share): set by the overlap between plan.ksbs_due entries with due_by on or before the review date and progress.ksbs_signed codes. extra_unplanned_ksbs_signed adds signed codes that are not yet due; these must not count.

Mitigation (mitigation_present, p 0.5): the alarming signal, such as low hours or a run of absences, appears equally often with and without it.
- approved_break_in_learning: an approved:true entry in plan.breaks.
- documented_medical_absence: absences with reason_code "MED", authorised:true and a cert_ref.
- employer_shutdown_window: employer_input.shutdown_from and shutdown_to overlap the period.
- hours_pending_verification: progress.otj_pending_hrs is large. Logged hours already include pending hours, so the shortfall scale is unchanged, but pending hours point to hold_evidence rather than support_plan.

slippage_cause shows up through comparisons, never through a label:
- apprentice: unauthorised absences, or few signed KSBs despite sessions held.
- employer: employer_input.otj_hrs_released below the hours needed, or workplace_tasks_assigned low.
- provider: attendance.sessions_cancelled_by_provider high, or ksbs whose evidence dates passed but which are unsigned.
- mixed: two of these at similar strength.

Missing or out-of-order items:
- employer_input_missing: employer_input is null, employer_attended is false and signatures.mentor is null.
- signoff_out_of_order: a signature date earlier than review_date.
- functional skills: booked_no_result shows exam_date set and result null; not_started shows both null.

weeks_to_gateway is the gap between apprentice.planned_gateway and review_date.

prior_reviews_with_actions sets the count of review_meeting.prior_reviews entries with outcome_code ACT or SUP.

Decoys:
- unit_grades: high grades.
- mentor_changed_on: a recent date.
- many_absences_all_authorised: authorised absences with no shortfall.
- extra_unplanned_ksbs_signed: signed KSBs not yet due.
None of these alone justifies concern.

boundary_case places values on a threshold, for example exactly 85% of due KSBs, a 10.0% shortfall, or a shortfall near 25% before pending hours are counted, so that judges may split.

gateway_on_track holds only when all of the following are true:
- the KSB share is at least 85%;
- the shortfall is under 10%;
- functional skills are passed, exempt, or booked with an exam_date before planned_gateway;
- the gateway date has not passed.

review_disposition:
- hold_evidence: exactly one missing signature, record or verification.
- refer_manager: a severe shortfall or KSB share under 50% with two or more prior action reviews, or a gateway date already passed.

F228.domain: shipping container weight verification at a port
F228.role: VGM verification officer at a container terminal's export gate and yard planning desk
F228.setting: A container terminal checks each export container's shipper-declared verified gross mass (VGM) before it is released to vessel stowage. The officer reviews one container record at a time. Each record holds the shipper's declaration, the container's equipment data, the shipper's cargo lines, the terminal's own weighbridge reading, the voyage and stowage plan, and the shipper's history. The officer derives the terminal gross mass and compares it with the declaration. They decide whether the declaration is understated, what happens to the container, which source explains any gap, how large the gap is, and how much time pressure applies before loading.

vgm_understated.instructions: Latest declared VGM understates valid terminal-derived mass beyond permitted tolerance.

criteria.true: Valid terminal mass exceeds latest declared VGM beyond tolerance.
criteria.false: Within tolerance, overstated, or terminal reading not valid.

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this container before vessel loading?

criteria.release: Latest declared VGM accepted; container proceeds to stowage unchanged.
criteria.amend_and_load: Valid terminal mass replaces declared VGM; container loads this voyage.
criteria.hold_reweigh: Container held in yard awaiting reweigh, recalibration or missing documents.
criteria.shut_out: Container removed from this sailing; mass unacceptable or cutoff missed.

gap_source.instructions: Which single source mainly explains any weight gap found?

criteria.no_material_gap: Gap under 2%, so no source needs attributing.
criteria.tare_error: Declared container tare differs from the CSC plate tare.
criteria.cargo_error: Declared cargo mass disagrees with the summed cargo lines.
criteria.weighing_error: Terminal reading unreliable: lapsed calibration or wrong chassis tare.

gap_magnitude.instructions: How large is the gap between declared and terminal mass?
criteria: Absolute gap under 2% of declared VGM
Absolute gap 2% to under 5% of declared VGM
Absolute gap 5% to under 10% of declared VGM
Absolute gap 10% or more of declared VGM

time_pressure.instructions: How much time pressure applies before this container's planned loading?
criteria: Relaxed: planned loading more than 48 hours away
Planned: planned loading 12 to 48 hours away
Pressing: planned loading 2 to under 12 hours away
Critical: under 2 hours, or loading already started

factors.name: gap_band
factors.description: Size of the absolute gap between terminal-derived gross mass and the original declared VGM. Some draws land within 0.2 percentage points of the 2%, 5% or 10% anchors.

factors.name: gap_direction
factors.description: Whether terminal mass exceeds the declaration (understated) or falls below it (overstated).

factors.name: gap_source
factors.description: Which section the material gap traces to: declared tare against the plate, declared cargo against the cargo lines, or a terminal weighing fault.

factors.name: decoy_mismatch
factors.description: Trivial cross-section inconsistency that does not explain the gap.

factors.name: scale_calibration_valid
factors.description: Whether the weighbridge calibration certificate was in date at the reading time. A lapsed certificate invalidates the terminal reading.

factors.name: amended_vgm_on_file
factors.description: Mitigation: the shipper filed a corrected VGM before cutoff that matches terminal mass within tolerance.

factors.name: shipper_trusted
factors.description: Mitigation: the shipper is an authorised Method 2 weigher with a clean audit in the last 12 months.

factors.name: prior_discrepancies
factors.description: Count of VGM discrepancies logged against this shipper in the past 12 months.

factors.name: hours_to_loading
factors.description: Hours from the review timestamp to the planned loading start. Some draws sit exactly on the 2, 12 or 48 hour anchors, and some are negative (loading already started).

factors.name: reweigh_status
factors.description: State of any second weighing.

factors.name: stow_position
factors.description: Planned stowage location; high deck tiers make an understated mass more consequential.

factors.name: exceeds_csc_max
factors.description: Whether terminal-derived mass exceeds the CSC plate maximum gross mass.

factors.name: cargo_lines_missing
factors.description: Whether the cargo_lines section is absent or null, preventing a cargo-side cross-check.

factors.name: tolerance_pct
factors.description: Terminal policy tolerance applied to VGM gaps for this service.

sections.name: booking_declaration
sections.description: Shipper VGM submission: booking_ref, container_no, vgm_kg, declared_tare_kg, declared_cargo_kg, method, signatory_id, submitted_at, and an amendments list of {vgm_kg, submitted_at}.

sections.name: equipment
sections.description: Container data: container_no, iso_type, csc_plate_tare_kg, csc_max_gross_kg, seal_no.

sections.name: cargo_lines
sections.description: Shipper cargo list of {hs_code, packages, package_type, gross_kg}; may be null.

sections.name: terminal_weighing
sections.description: Gate weighbridge data: scale_id, read_at, gross_reading_kg, tractor_tare_kg, chassis_tare_kg, chassis_registry_tare_kg, calibration_valid_to, plus a reweigh object {status, gross_reading_kg, read_at}.

sections.name: voyage_plan
sections.description: Vessel and stowage: vessel_code, voyage_no, vgm_cutoff_at, loading_start_at, review_at, stow_bay_row_tier, deck_or_hold, tolerance_pct.

sections.name: shipper_profile
sections.description: Shipper standing: shipper_id, method2_authorised, last_audit_on, last_audit_result, discrepancies_12m.

F228.rendering_notes: No field states the gap, its percentage, the source, a risk level or a recommended action. The reader must derive terminal mass as gross_reading_kg minus tractor_tare_kg minus chassis_tare_kg, or use reweigh.gross_reading_kg when a completed reweigh exists. Gap and gap_magnitude are measured against the original vgm_kg in booking_declaration. vgm_understated is judged against the latest amendment if one exists, otherwise against vgm_kg. The gap_band and gap_direction factors set the difference between derived terminal mass and vgm_kg. The gap_source factor places the cause. For tare, declared_tare_kg differs from csc_plate_tare_kg by roughly the gap. For cargo, declared_cargo_kg differs from the sum of cargo_lines gross_kg, while that sum plus plate tare matches terminal mass. For weighing, either calibration_valid_to precedes read_at or chassis_tare_kg differs from chassis_registry_tare_kg, so declared figures reconcile with cargo lines and plate. When the gap is under 2% the source is not material and gap_source is no_material_gap. The decoy_mismatch factor adds a trivial inconsistency elsewhere: packages off by one with unchanged weight, a sub-40 kg tare difference, a different timezone offset on timestamps, or a seal suffix differing between equipment and declaration. When scale_calibration_valid is false, calibration_valid_to is set before read_at; the terminal reading is then invalid, so vgm_understated is false unless a completed reweigh exists. When amended_vgm_on_file is true, the amendments list holds an entry before vgm_cutoff_at matching terminal mass within tolerance_pct. The shipper_trusted factor shows as method2_authorised true with a last_audit_on within 12 months and a pass result. prior_discrepancies appears as discrepancies_12m. hours_to_loading is the difference between loading_start_at and review_at; it is never given as a number. reweigh_status fills the reweigh object, with status requested and null readings for requested_not_done. stow_position is encoded in stow_bay_row_tier and deck_or_hold. When exceeds_csc_max is true, derived terminal mass is above csc_max_gross_kg, which should drive shut_out. When cargo_lines_missing is true, cargo_lines is null. tolerance_pct sits in voyage_plan. Mitigating fields appear with and without alarming gaps about equally. Disposition guide: release when the gap is within tolerance or a matching amendment is on file. Use amend_and_load for a valid reading beyond tolerance, within plate maximum, with time remaining. Use hold_reweigh for an invalid calibration, a requested reweigh not yet done, or missing cargo lines with a gap beyond tolerance. Use shut_out when plate maximum is exceeded, or when loading has started with a large unresolved gap. Boundary gaps, trusted shippers with a moderate gap on a high deck tier, and readings exactly at tolerance are deliberately contestable.

F229.role: Press-house lot reviewer at a winery, checking each pressing lot log before its juice is released from settling to fermentation
F229.setting: During vintage, each fruit delivery is weighed, sampled, pressed and pumped to a settling tank. The reviewer works through one lot log at a time and compares the vineyard pick record, weighbridge ticket, intake sample, press cycle and tank transfer. Problems include weights that do not reconcile, juice yields that do not fit the press programme, identifiers that change between stages, missing steps, out-of-order timestamps and long gaps between picking and pressing. Operator notes may explain a discrepancy or contradict the logged data.

yield_consistent.instructions: Juice yield reconciles with the net fruit weight recorded at intake.

criteria.true: Litres per tonne fall inside the programme's stated band
criteria.false: Yield outside band, or net weight fails to reconcile

chain_intact.instructions: Lot and block identifiers carry through unchanged from intake to tank.

release_decision.instructions: What should happen next to this lot's pressed juice?

criteria.release: No discrepancies found; juice moves to its logged tank.
criteria.release_corrected: Only clerical mismatches; fix record, juice moves on regardless.
criteria.hold: One confirmation outstanding, no fault confirmed; juice stays settling.
criteria.segregate: Fruit or process fault found; isolate juice from intended blend.

pick_press_delay.instructions: How long did fruit wait between end of picking and pressing?
criteria: Prompt: press started under 4 hours after picking ended
Standard: 4 to under 8 hours after picking ended
Delayed: 8 to under 16 hours after picking ended
Overnight: 16 hours or more after picking ended

failed_checks.instructions: How many of the standard checks on this record failed?
criteria: No standard checks failed
Exactly one standard check failed
Two or three standard checks failed
Four or more standard checks failed

factors.name: weight_mismatch
factors.description: Discrepancy between weighbridge gross minus tare and the recorded net_kg, or between the bin count and the summed bin weights

factors.name: press_programme
factors.description: Press programme used, which sets the expected litres-per-tonne band shown in the press section

factors.name: yield_position
factors.description: Where the actual juice litres per tonne of net fruit sit relative to the programme band

factors.name: lot_id_drift
factors.description: Whether the lot or block identifier changes between the pick record, weighbridge ticket, press log and tank transfer

factors.name: missing_step
factors.description: A required step or section is absent or null, such as the intake sample, the SO2 addition, the press cycle end or the QA sign-off

factors.name: out_of_order_timestamp
factors.description: A timestamp sequence is impossible, for example a sample taken after the press started or a press start before weighbridge arrival

factors.name: pick_to_press_hours
factors.description: True hours from end of picking to press cycle start, derived from the pick record and the press log

factors.name: pick_end_recorded
factors.description: Whether the pick record carries a pick_end time; if absent, only the weighbridge arrival bounds the delay

factors.name: cold_held
factors.description: Mitigation: fruit was held in the cold room before pressing, shown by low intake temperature and a cold-room entry

factors.name: rot_pct
factors.description: Bunch rot percentage in the intake sample

factors.name: sorting_applied
factors.description: Mitigation: fruit passed over the sorting table, with a post-sort rot figure and rejected-kg logged

factors.name: note_signal
factors.description: What the free-text notes contribute: nothing relevant, a benign decoy, a claim that contradicts logged data, or an explanation that resolves a mismatch

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Places one key value exactly on a threshold, such as a delay of exactly 8.0 hours or a yield at the band limit

sections.name: lot
sections.description: Lot id, vineyard block code, variety, crew, pick_date, pick_start, pick_end (nullable)

sections.name: intake
sections.description: Weighbridge ticket: ticket_no, block_code, arrival_at, gross_kg, tare_kg, net_kg, bins list, temp_c, cold_room_in/out, driver_note

sections.name: sample
sections.description: Intake sample: sampled_at, brix, ph, ta_g_l, rot_pct, mog_pct, sort block (sorted, rejected_kg, post_sort_rot_pct); may be null

sections.name: press
sections.description: Press cycle: press_id, programme, band_l_per_t, cycle_start, cycle_end, free_run_l, press_fraction_l, juice_l, so2_mg_l, operator_note

sections.name: transfer
sections.description: Tank transfer: lot_ref, tank_id, transferred_l, transferred_at, qa_signoff (initials/time or null), qa_comment

F229.rendering_notes: weight_mismatch appears only as raw numbers: gross_kg, tare_kg, net_kg and per-bin kg in intake.bins; the reader must do the arithmetic. press_programme sets press.programme and press.band_l_per_t (for example '600-680'); yield_position is reflected through juice_l against net_kg and is never stated as a ratio. transferred_l may differ slightly from juice_l as a decoy within normal lees loss. lot_id_drift alters lot.lot_id, intake.block_code, transfer.lot_ref or the tank log id at one stage only. missing_step renders as a null section (sample: null), a null field (cycle_end, so2_mg_l, qa_signoff) or an omitted key. out_of_order_timestamp shifts sampled_at, cycle_start or arrival_at so the sequence is impossible. pick_to_press_hours comes from lot.pick_end and press.cycle_start; when pick_end_recorded is false, pick_end is null and only intake.arrival_at gives a lower bound, which may leave the delay level contested. cold_held renders as intake.temp_c of 4-8 with cold_room_in and cold_room_out times, otherwise temp_c of 16-30 and null cold-room fields. rot_pct goes in sample.rot_pct; sorting_applied fills sample.sort with rejected_kg and post_sort_rot_pct, which net_kg may or may not already reflect. Free text (driver_note, operator_note, qa_comment) is one sentence each. A contradicting note claims something the log disproves, such as 'sorted on table' with a null sort block, or names another tank. An explaining note accounts for a mismatch, such as 'bin 7 reweighed, ticket amended'. Benign decoys mention weather, a crew change or minor press noise. No record contains a delay figure, a yield ratio, a release status, a risk rating or a pass/fail field; the reviewer must derive every answer from the compared values.

F230.role: Deputy care home manager (registered nurse) auditing one resident's completed medication round record the following morning
F230.setting: A residential and nursing care home keeps an electronic medication administration record. Each morning the deputy manager audits completed rounds one resident at a time. Each record joins the resident's details, current prescriptions and amendments, the doses signed during the round, item stock counts, round details with open queries and post-dose observations, and a short error history. The reviewer must decide whether the record closes cleanly, needs correcting, is held for confirmation, or triggers an incident report or clinical escalation.

dose_mismatch.instructions: A dose given this round differed from the prescription in force.

stock_reconciles.instructions: Every item's closing stock reconciles with opening, receipts and signed doses.

criteria.true: Each closing count equals expected after recorded movements
criteria.false: At least one closing count differs from expected

next_step.instructions: What should the reviewer do with this round record next?

criteria.sign_off: No discrepancies found; record is complete and can close.
criteria.correct_and_close: Recording slip only; amend with annotation, then close record.
criteria.hold: One open query must be answered before outcome is decided.
criteria.report_incident: Confirmed error on an ordinary drug; file internal incident report.
criteria.clinical_escalation: Confirmed error on time-critical or high-risk drug; seek GP advice.

open_discrepancies.instructions: How many items still have an unresolved discrepancy after review?
criteria: No item has an unresolved discrepancy
Exactly one item has an unresolved discrepancy
Two or three items have unresolved discrepancies
Four or more items have unresolved discrepancies

error_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst error found in this round?
criteria: None: every dose correct or validly withheld
Documentation: dose correct but signature or code missing
Timing: correct dose given over 60 minutes late
Dose: ordinary drug omitted, duplicated or wrong strength
Critical: time-critical drug omitted, duplicated or wrong strength

factors.name: dose_mismatch_type
factors.description: Whether and how units_given in an administration entry departs from the prescribed dose_units for that item

factors.name: prescription_change_documented
factors.description: Whether a dated amendment with an order reference makes the apparently mismatched dose correct for this round

factors.name: omission_count
factors.description: Number of scheduled doses with no administration entry or a not-given code

factors.name: omission_reason_valid
factors.description: Whether omissions carry a code backed elsewhere, such as resident status hospital or a withhold order

factors.name: late_minutes
factors.description: Largest gap in minutes between scheduled and given_at time across the round

factors.name: time_critical_affected
factors.description: Whether the item carrying the worst error is flagged time_critical or high_risk in prescriptions

factors.name: stock_variance
factors.description: Closing count minus expected count for the most discrepant item; zero means reconciled

factors.name: stock_variance_explained
factors.description: Whether a witnessed wasted or returned movement in stock accounts for the variance

factors.name: signature_gaps
factors.description: Number of administration entries missing initials, or missing second initials for controlled drugs

factors.name: unit_expression_decoy
factors.description: How a correct dose is expressed: same units as prescribed, or an equivalent split such as two 5 mg tablets for 10 mg

factors.name: post_dose_obs_reassuring
factors.description: Whether a post-dose observation (blood glucose, pulse, INR due date) after the error lies within normal range

factors.name: pending_query
factors.description: Open query on the round whose answer would change the outcome

factors.name: prior_errors_30d
factors.description: Count of medication incidents for this resident in the past 30 days; context only, never decisive

factors.name: item_count
factors.description: Number of prescribed items on the round, setting how many places discrepancies can hide

sections.name: resident
sections.description: Resident id, room, dob, weight_kg, allergies list, status and status_since date

sections.name: prescriptions
sections.description: List of items: item_id, drug, strength_mg, form, dose_units, times, prn, time_critical, high_risk, controlled, changes list

sections.name: administrations
sections.description: List of entries: item_id, scheduled, given_at, units_given, strength_mg_used, code, initials, second_initials

sections.name: stock
sections.description: Per item: opening, received, wasted, wasted_witnessed, returned, closing

sections.name: round
sections.description: Round_id, date, slot, started, finished, staff_on, open_queries list, post_dose_obs list

sections.name: history
sections.description: Errors_30d, refusals_7d, last_audit date, last_audit_passed boolean

F230.rendering_notes: prescriptions holds item_count items; administrations has one entry per scheduled dose. dose_mismatch_type shows only as units_given or strength_mg_used differing from the matching prescription item, or a second entry for the same item_id and scheduled time; it is never labelled. prescription_change_documented appears as a changes entry {effective, new_dose_units, order_ref, authorised_by_role}; when false, either no change exists or the effective date falls after the round date or order_ref is null. omission_count shows as missing entries or code values R, H, W, N or O with units_given 0; omission_reason_valid is true only when the code is supported elsewhere (H with resident.status hospital and status_since before the round; W with a changes entry carrying a withhold order_ref); a code alone does not count. late_minutes is derived from scheduled versus given_at; place values near 60 regularly to create boundary cases. time_critical_affected is the time_critical or high_risk flag on the erroneous item. stock_variance shows as closing differing from opening + received - wasted - returned - doses signed; stock_variance_explained true adds a wasted or returned amount equal to the gap with wasted_witnessed true; a wasted amount with wasted_witnessed false is a contested case. signature_gaps shows as null initials, or null second_initials on a controlled item. unit_expression_decoy: equivalent_split records units_given 2 with strength_mg_used 5 against a 10 mg prescription, which is correct and not a mismatch. post_dose_obs_reassuring appears in round.post_dose_obs as a numeric value within or outside normal range for its type, with no range label. pending_query appears in round.open_queries with type, raised timestamp and item_id; none means an empty list. prior_errors_30d, refusals_7d and last_audit_passed are decoys giving context and never decide an answer. Decoys also include allergies (never matching a prescribed drug), weight_kg and staff_on. No field states an error, severity, discrepancy, reconciliation result or recommended action; records contain no free-text fields, only codes, numbers, ISO timestamps, booleans and nulls.

F231.domain: film location permit applications to a council
F231.role: Council filming liaison officer reviewing location permit applications
F231.setting: A local council's filming office receives applications from production companies wanting to shoot on streets, parks and council property. The liaison officer reviews one application record at a time. Each record holds the applicant's history, the shoot schedule, the location footprint, compliance documents, resident consultation and the council booking calendar. For each record the officer decides whether insurance and consultation requirements are met, what should happen to the application next, and how much public highway disruption the shoot involves.

insurance_valid.instructions: Public liability cover meets the council minimum across every shoot date.

criteria.true: Cover amount and validity dates span the whole shoot
criteria.false: Cover short, missing, or lapses before final wrap

consultation_met.instructions: All required streets were notified within the lead time or waived.

criteria.true: Every listed street notified on time or waiver held
criteria.false: Notice late without waiver, unlogged, or streets missed

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this permit application next?

criteria.refuse: Reject because a blocking conflict or breach cannot be remedied
criteria.request_info: Pause until one missing document or confirmation is supplied
criteria.approve_conditions: Grant with added limits on hours, area, staffing or marshals
criteria.approve: Grant as submitted with only the standard permit terms

recurrence_count.instructions: How often has this same issue been logged in 12 months?
criteria: First occurrence; not logged in prior 12 months
Logged once before within the past 12 months
Logged two to four times in 12 months
Logged five or more times in 12 months

highway_impact.instructions: How much of the public highway does the shoot occupy?
criteria: No highway use; private land or parks only
Pavement or parking bays used, carriageway left open
Intermittent traffic holds, carriageway never fully closed
Full road closure on at least one shoot date

factors.name: shoot_scale
factors.description: Size of the unit, shown through crew size and unit vehicle count; it shapes conditions but does not decide them alone

factors.name: highway_use
factors.description: Extent of public highway occupation, which sets the true highway_impact level

factors.name: insurance_status
