factors.description: State of public liability cover compared with the council minimum and the shoot dates

factors.name: renewal_confirmed
factors.description: An insurer renewal confirmation is on file, which mitigates expiry before wrap but is not itself a certificate

factors.name: notification_state
factors.description: How the resident notification was carried out relative to the required lead time and street list

factors.name: lead_time_waiver
factors.description: An approved short-notice waiver reference exists, which excuses late notification but does not cover missed streets

factors.name: event_clash
factors.description: Another booking on the council calendar overlaps the same street and date

factors.name: clash_consent
factors.description: The organiser of the clashing booking has given written consent on file, which lowers the conflict to a condition

factors.name: tmp_status
factors.description: Traffic management plan status; it is required when the carriageway is held or closed

factors.name: submission_lead_days
factors.description: Days between the submission date and the first shoot date; negative values mean the application was submitted after filming started

factors.name: prior_complaints
factors.description: Number of logged complaints against the applicant in the last 12 months, some of the same category

factors.name: night_filming
factors.description: Shoot runs past 23:00 on some dates; this pushes towards conditions unless consultation is clean

sections.name: applicant
sections.description: Production company reference, prior permit count and a list of 12-month complaint entries

sections.name: schedule
sections.description: Submission date and a list of shoot dates with call and wrap times

sections.name: location
sections.description: Site type, street references, crew size, unit vehicles and highway occupation details

sections.name: compliance
sections.description: Insurance cover and dates, traffic management plan status and reference

sections.name: consultation
sections.description: Notice date, required lead days, waiver reference, required versus notified street lists, objection count

sections.name: council_calendar
sections.description: List of overlapping bookings with street, date and consent flag

F231.rendering_notes: No free-text fields; all values are codes, numbers, dates, booleans or null. shoot_scale appears as location.crew_size and location.unit_vehicles. highway_use appears only indirectly through location.highway.pavement_m, location.highway.parking_bays, location.highway.carriageway ('open','intermittent_hold','closed') and location.highway.hold_max_mins; for 'none', location.site_type is 'private_land' or 'park' and the highway block holds zeros. insurance_status appears as compliance.insurance.cover_gbp versus compliance.insurance.required_gbp, and compliance.insurance.valid_to versus the last schedule.shoot_dates date; certificate_missing renders the insurance object as null. renewal_confirmed appears as compliance.insurance.renewal_letter_on_file (true/false), present only when valid_to precedes wrap or set as a decoy otherwise. notification_state appears as consultation.notice_sent_on compared with the first shoot date minus consultation.required_lead_days, and consultation.streets_required compared with consultation.streets_notified; not_logged sets notice_sent_on to null and streets_notified to an empty list. lead_time_waiver appears as consultation.waiver_ref, a code string or null. event_clash appears as an entry in council_calendar.overlapping with matching street_ref and date; clash_consent is that entry's consent_on_file boolean. tmp_status appears as compliance.tmp.status with compliance.tmp.ref; 'absent' renders as null, and it matters only when the carriageway is held or closed. submission_lead_days appears as schedule.submitted_on against the first shoot date; a submission dated after filming starts is an out-of-order signal. prior_complaints appears as applicant.complaints_12m, a list of {logged_on, category} entries feeding the shared recurrence scale. night_filming appears as wrap_time values after 23:00 in schedule.shoot_dates. Decoys: a high applicant.prior_permits count, which does not offset problems; a large consultation.objections count when notification was correct; a large pavement_m with an open carriageway; crew_size that is high on private land; and a renewal_letter_on_file flag that is true when cover is already valid. No field may state the permit decision, the impact level, compliance pass or fail, or any risk rating; the record shows only what an applicant portal and council systems would hold.

F232.role: Duty support astronomer reviewing each telescope night's observing log the following morning, deciding how the night is charged to the programme and what follow-up is needed
F232.setting: A fictional mountain-top observatory, Cerro Lumbrera, runs a 2.4 m telescope with an imaging camera on queue and visitor programmes. After each night, the duty support astronomer opens one night log record. Each record combines the night header, the weather and dome-closure record, the list of exposures taken, the programme's requested targets and constraints, and the engineering fault list, together with short notes from the observer and night assistant. The reviewer must reconcile these sections, weigh alarming entries against mitigating context and decide on time accounting and engineering follow-up. The same five decisions are made for every night, whatever happened.

weather_only_loss.instructions: All time lost this night is attributable to weather, not equipment.

criteria.true: Every lost interval matches a supported weather closure.
criteria.false: Some lost time overlaps faults or lacks supported cause.

claims_supported.instructions: Logged exposures support every target completion claimed in the observer note.

criteria.true: Each claimed target has required filters and exposure total.
criteria.false: A claimed completion lacks a filter or enough exposure.

night_disposition.instructions: How should this night be charged and followed up?

criteria.charge_full: All allocated hours charged; no time lost to any cause.
criteria.charge_partial: Weather losses returned to pool; completed data stands, no repeats.
criteria.hold: Charging deferred until one pending QA or ticket confirmation arrives.
criteria.requeue_targets: Technical loss left named targets incomplete; repeat only those.
criteria.reschedule_night: Technical loss exceeded half the allocation; request a replacement night.

usable_share.instructions: What share of allocated time yielded usable science exposures?
criteria: None: no exposure passes QA within programme limits
Low: usable exposure time below 40% of allocation
Substantial: usable time from 40% to 80% of allocation
Full: usable time above 80% of allocation

fault_followup.instructions: How unresolved is the worst science-affecting fault from the night?
criteria: No science-affecting fault, or fault cleared and retested
Fault cleared, but no retest entry logged yet
Fault still open; logged workaround kept observing possible
Fault still open; no workaround, instrument unusable

factors.name: weather_loss_hours
factors.description: Hours of dome closure genuinely caused by weather (humidity, wind or cloud above limits), shown as closure intervals in conditions.closures and supported by weather station readings.

factors.name: fault_overlap
factors.description: Whether engineering fault intervals overlap dome-open time when science could have run: none, a short overlap under 30 minutes, or a major overlap of an hour or more.

factors.name: fault_resolution_state
factors.description: State of the worst fault in faults list: none logged, cleared with retest entry, cleared without retest, open with a workaround noted, or open and blocking.

factors.name: maintenance_window
factors.description: Whether the fault occurred inside a scheduled engineering window recorded in night_header.eng_window, so it carries no science loss despite looking alarming.

factors.name: closure_reason_mismatch
factors.description: Whether a closure logged with reason 'weather' is contradicted by weather station readings below limits during that interval, or by a fault starting at the same time.

factors.name: note_claim_discrepancy
factors.description: Gap between targets the observer note calls complete and the exposures logged: none, a required filter missing, exposure total short by under 10%, or short by 10% or more.

factors.name: seeing_vs_limit
factors.description: Median seeing during science exposures relative to programme max_seeing_arcsec: well within, within 0.1 arcsec of the limit, or exceeded.

factors.name: seeing_exception_approved
factors.description: Whether programme_request carries an approved relaxed seeing limit for some targets, making frames that breach the default limit still usable.

factors.name: usable_fraction
factors.description: True fraction of allocated hours yielding usable science exposure time (QA pass, within constraints); must be computed from exposures and allocation, never stated.

factors.name: qa_pending_count
factors.description: Number of science exposures whose qa field is null (pipeline not yet run), which can leave charging awaiting one confirmation.

factors.name: utc_date_rollover
factors.description: Whether exposures cross UTC midnight so their dates differ from the local night date in the header; a decoy that looks like a date mismatch but is not.

factors.name: assistant_note_tone
factors.description: Night assistant note: neutral, alarming but explained elsewhere (e.g. noise from scheduled test), or alarming and matching a real open fault.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether one deciding value is placed exactly on a scale threshold (usable share at 40% or 80%, technical loss at half the allocation, seeing equal to limit) so judges may split.

sections.name: night_header
sections.description: Local night date, telescope, instrument, programme_id, allocated_hours, twilight times and any eng_window interval.

sections.name: conditions
sections.description: Weather station summaries per hour and a closures list with start, end and logged reason.

sections.name: exposures
sections.description: List of frames: frame_id, target_id, start_utc, exptime_s, filter, airmass, seeing_arcsec, qa (pass, fail or null).

sections.name: programme_request
sections.description: Requested targets with required filters, total exposure seconds, max_seeing_arcsec, max_airmass and any approved exception.

sections.name: faults
sections.description: Engineering entries: subsystem, start_utc, end_utc or null, cleared, retest_utc or null, workaround text or null, ticket_ref.

sections.name: notes
sections.description: Two short free-text fields: observer_note naming targets completed and night_assistant_note.

F232.rendering_notes: weather_loss_hours appears as conditions.closures intervals with reason 'weather' and hourly station values (humidity_pct, wind_kmh, cloud_okta) above limits given in conditions.limits. closure_reason_mismatch is shown only by station values below limits during a 'weather' closure, or by a faults entry whose start_utc falls within two minutes of the closure start. fault_overlap is rendered through faults start/end versus times when no closure is active and exposures are absent. fault_resolution_state maps to cleared, retest_utc and workaround fields; maintenance_window places the fault inside night_header.eng_window (null when absent). note_claim_discrepancy is visible only by summing exptime_s per target and filter in exposures against programme_request totals for targets the observer_note calls 'done' or 'complete'; small shortfalls should look like rounding. seeing_vs_limit appears in per-frame seeing_arcsec against max_seeing_arcsec; seeing_exception_approved appears as programme_request.exception with target_ids and relaxed_seeing_arcsec, null when absent. usable_fraction is never stated; reviewers derive it from qa-pass, in-constraint exptime_s against allocated_hours. qa_pending_count frames have qa null. utc_date_rollover gives exposures start_utc dates one day after the header's local date: a decoy, not an error. assistant_note_tone drives night_assistant_note wording (e.g. 'loud grinding from dome drive around 02:10'), which for alarmed_benign is explained by an eng_window test, and for alarmed_real matches an open fault. Decoys: rollover dates, alarming notes, seeing breaches covered by exceptions, faults inside the engineering window. Records must never contain fields such as 'charge', 'usable_pct', 'disposition', 'loss_cause' or 'severity'; all answers come from comparing sections. Some records should have no mismatches at all.

F233.domain: medical tent logs at a marathon
F233.role: Medical tent shift lead at a city marathon, reviewing each runner encounter log before it is signed off and filed
F233.setting: Each record is the encounter log for one runner treated in a finish-line or course medical tent. It holds the runner's registration details, arrival and triage entry, timed observation sets, treatments given and the discharge entry. The shift lead checks the log for consistency and completeness, judges how unwell the runner was and what condition they presented with, and decides whether the log can be filed or needs follow-up.

heat_stroke_supported.instructions: The recorded observations support exertional heat stroke as working diagnosis.

review_action.instructions: What is the highest action this log warrants at shift review?

criteria.sign_off: Log complete and consistent across sections; file without further action.
criteria.hold_for_query: Entry missing, unsigned or conflicting; query treating clinician before filing.
criteria.recall_runner: Runner left before release criteria met; arrange welfare contact today.
criteria.escalate_to_director: Recorded care may have missed a critical condition; director reviews urgently.

presentation_category.instructions: Which condition category best fits the runner's primary presentation?

criteria.minor_skin: Blisters, chafing or abrasions only, with normal vitals throughout.
criteria.musculoskeletal: Cramp, strain or sprain without collapse or abnormal vitals.
criteria.postural_collapse: Collapse at or after finish, normal core temperature and sodium.
criteria.heat_illness: Core temperature 39.0°C or above, sodium normal or untested.
criteria.sodium_disturbance: Point-of-care sodium below 135 mmol/L, whatever the temperature.

obs_completeness.instructions: How complete is the set of recorded observations for this stay?
criteria: None: no observation set recorded during the stay.
Arrival only: one set on arrival, never repeated.
Partial: repeat sets logged but no pre-discharge set.
Complete: arrival, repeat and pre-discharge sets all logged.

worst_consciousness.instructions: What was the worst level of consciousness recorded during the stay?
criteria: Alert and oriented at every recorded check.
Alert but confused or disoriented at least once.
Responded only to voice or pain at least once.
Unresponsive at one or more recorded checks.

factors.name: presentation_type
factors.description: True underlying presentation driving the encounter; shapes vitals, sodium, temperature, treatments and the presenting complaint code, which may be vaguer than the true type.

factors.name: heat_severity
factors.description: For heat presentations, peak core temperature band: below 39, 39.0 to 39.9, or 40.0 and above; non-heat cases mostly normal.

factors.name: temp_site
factors.description: Site used for the peak temperature reading; tympanic and oral under-read after running, so a high tympanic value alone does not establish core temperature.

factors.name: worst_avpu
factors.description: Worst consciousness state actually recorded in any observation set, which may differ from the arrival triage entry.

factors.name: obs_coverage
factors.description: Which observation phases were logged: none, arrival only, arrival plus repeats without pre-discharge, or full coverage.

factors.name: cross_section_mismatch
factors.description: Unannounced disagreement between sections: none, trivial clock drift under five minutes, bib differs between runner and arrival, triage AVPU disagrees with first observation set, arrival temperature differs from first set, or treatment fluid volumes do not sum to discharge total.

factors.name: early_departure
factors.description: Runner left before release criteria were met: discharge left_at precedes pre-discharge obs, disposition is self_discharged, or abnormal last vitals at departure.

factors.name: departure_mitigated
factors.description: Lowers concern about departure: runner accompanied by named companion, handed to ambulance crew, or advice sheet acknowledged; drawn independently of early_departure.

factors.name: sodium_tested
factors.description: Whether a point-of-care sodium was taken; when false sodium_mmol is null, so a sodium disturbance cannot be confirmed.

factors.name: cooling_explains_temp
factors.description: Mitigation for a high reading: the high value was tympanic or taken mid-run, and a rectal reading on arrival or soon after was normal; or temperature normalised after documented ice-water immersion.

factors.name: out_of_order_care
factors.description: A timestamp shows care happened out of sequence: treatment given before arrived_at, or saline infusion logged before a low sodium result was noted.

factors.name: declared_condition
factors.description: Runner's registration lists a condition or medication that explains an abnormal sign, such as beta-blocker for low heart rate or diabetes for low glucose.

factors.name: borderline_value
factors.description: A deciding value sits exactly on a threshold: temperature 39.0 or 40.0, sodium 135, or GCS 14 with AVPU alert.

factors.name: discharge_signed
factors.description: Whether the discharge entry carries a clinician signature; when false signed_by is null or the discharge section is null.

sections.name: runner
sections.description: Registration details: bib, age_band, sex, start_wave, declared medical_flags list and medications list.

sections.name: arrival
sections.description: Tent entry: tent_id, bib, arrived_at, course_km, arrival_mode, complaint_code, triage_cat, avpu_on_arrival, temp_on_arrival_c.

sections.name: observations
sections.description: List of timed sets: taken_at, phase, hr, sbp, rr, spo2, temp_c, temp_site, avpu, gcs, glucose_mmol, sodium_mmol.

sections.name: treatment
sections.description: List of interventions: given_at, code, volume_ml, duration_min, by_role.

sections.name: discharge
sections.description: Exit entry: left_at, disposition, accompanied, fluids_total_ml, release_checklist booleans, signed_by; may be null.

F233.rendering_notes: presentation_type shows indirectly through complaint_code (collapse, cramp, blister, unwell, confused), vitals, temp_c, sodium_mmol and treatment codes (dressing, stretch_massage, leg_elevation, ice_water_immersion, oral_fluids, iv_saline_0_9, hypertonic_saline); complaint_code is a decoy and is often vaguer than or different from the true category. heat_severity sets the peak temp_c in observations and temp_on_arrival_c; temp_site sits on each set. worst_avpu appears only in observations[].avpu and gcs; arrival.avpu_on_arrival and arrival.triage_cat (P1 to P3) are decoys that may disagree with it. obs_coverage controls which phase values (arrival, repeat, pre_discharge) appear in observations; the list may be empty. cross_section_mismatch is never flagged: compare runner.bib with arrival.bib, avpu_on_arrival with the first set, temp_on_arrival_c with the first temp_c, summed treatment volume_ml with discharge.fluids_total_ml, and timestamps across sections. early_departure shows via left_at against pre_discharge taken_at, disposition self_discharged, or abnormal final vitals; departure_mitigated via accompanied true, disposition ambulance_transfer, or release_checklist.advice_given true. sodium_tested false renders sodium_mmol null in every set. cooling_explains_temp renders a later or adjacent rectal reading below 38.5 or an immersion entry followed by normal temp. out_of_order_care shows only through given_at earlier than arrived_at or iv_saline_0_9 given_at after a low sodium taken_at. declared_condition appears in runner.medical_flags or medications. discharge_signed false renders signed_by null or discharge null. Heat stroke is supported only when a rectal temp_c of 40.0 or above coincides, in the same or adjacent set, with avpu other than alert; tympanic highs alone or merely possible cases are false. Review action is the highest applicable step. No field may state a diagnosis, completeness level, review action, worst consciousness summary, risk rating or mismatch flag; disposition and triage_cat are genuine system fields and do not answer any question.

F234.role: Germination test reviewer at a conservation seed bank, signing off one completed germination test record per accession before its viability figure is updated
F234.setting: A national wild-plant seed bank holds thousands of accessions in long-term frozen storage. Each accession is periodically sampled and germination-tested on agar under a set protocol. The reviewer opens one test record at a time. They check the replicate counts against the sown numbers and the summary percentage. They check the seed drawn against the inventory, and the incubator log against the test window. They compare the result with earlier tests, then decide whether the result stands and what happens to the accession next.

result_valid.instructions: This test's result can be accepted as the accession's current viability.

criteria.true: Replicate counts reconcile, test complete, no unmitigated protocol breach.
criteria.false: Count gaps, unfinished test or unmitigated breach undermine the result.

next_step.instructions: What should happen next with this accession after the test?

criteria.accept: Record result as current viability; no further action now.
criteria.hold_query: Hold result pending one missing count, log or cut-test confirmation.
criteria.retest: Result unreliable; repeat the test on a fresh subsample.
criteria.regenerate: Valid result below regeneration threshold; schedule grow-out of accession.

shortfall_cause.instructions: Which single cause best explains the germination shortfall, if any?

criteria.none: Germination meets the accession's regeneration threshold; no shortfall to explain.
criteria.dormancy: Most non-germinated seeds were firm and fresh at test end.
criteria.deterioration: Most non-germinated seeds were dead or soft, indicating ageing.
criteria.test_artefact: Contamination or incubator deviations account for most seed losses.

discrepancy_size.instructions: How far does the recorded value differ from the expected value?
criteria: Matches expected value, or differs by under 2%
Differs from expected value by 2% to under 10%
Differs from expected value by 10% to under 25%
Differs from expected value by 25% or more

germ_decline.instructions: How far has germination fallen since the previous valid test?
criteria: Within 5 points of previous test, or higher
Fall of 6 to 15 percentage points
Fall of 16 to 30 percentage points
Fall of more than 30 percentage points

factors.name: true_viability_band
factors.description: Underlying viability of the accession, setting how many seeds can germinate when dormancy and artefacts are set aside.

factors.name: dormancy_fraction
factors.description: Share of sown seeds left firm and fresh but ungerminated at test end; this decides dormancy versus deterioration.

factors.name: count_gap_size
factors.description: Size of the mismatch between corresponding counts. Examples: replicate category totals against seeds sown, recorded summary percentage against the percentage computed from replicates, or seeds drawn against the inventory change.

factors.name: count_gap_location
factors.description: Where the count mismatch sits when there is one, so that gaps are never always in the same place.

factors.name: contamination_level
factors.description: Fungal or bacterial contamination recorded across replicates. This alarming signal can explain seed losses.

factors.name: contamination_mitigated
factors.description: Whether contamination is neutralised. It counts as neutralised if it was confined to one replicate excluded under protocol, or if affected seeds were transferred to fresh agar before death was scored.

factors.name: incubator_excursion
factors.description: Whether the incubator log shows a temperature or light excursion inside the test window.

factors.name: excursion_mitigated
factors.description: Whether the excursion is harmless. It counts as harmless if it fell under a logged maintenance ticket lasting under six hours, or if it occurred during cold pretreatment before seeds were moved into that cabinet.

factors.name: test_completion
factors.description: State of the test. It may have run to its scheduled end with the cut test done. It may have finished on time with the cut test of ungerminated seeds still outstanding. Or it may have been ended early.

factors.name: prior_decline_points
factors.description: Fall in germination percentage from the most recent previous valid test to this one. Negative values mean a rise.

factors.name: history_protocol_mismatch
factors.description: Whether the most recent history entry used a different protocol code. If so, the reviewer must compare against the last test under the same protocol instead.

factors.name: replicate_spread
factors.description: Heterogeneity of germination across replicates. High spread leaves the overall figure less certain.

factors.name: boundary_placement
factors.description: Whether key values are placed on a threshold edge, such as germination exactly at the regeneration threshold, a decline of exactly 15 or 16 points, or a dormant share near half of the non-germinated seeds.

sections.name: accession
sections.description: Accession id, taxon, collection date, storage temperature, regeneration threshold percentage and initial germination percentage.

sections.name: sample
sections.description: Seeds drawn for the test, inventory count before and after the draw, pretreatment code and dates.

sections.name: test
sections.description: Protocol code, medium, temperature regime, sow date, scheduled and actual end dates, cut-test date and recorded germination percentage.

sections.name: replicates
sections.description: List of replicates with sown, germinated, abnormal, fresh, dead, contaminated counts and an excluded flag.

sections.name: incubator
sections.description: Cabinet id and list of logged excursions with start, end, peak temperature and maintenance ticket reference or null.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Earlier germination tests with test date, protocol code and germination percentage.

F234.rendering_notes: true_viability_band drives replicates[].germinated relative to sown. dormancy_fraction appears as replicates[].fresh, with the remainder of the non-germinated seeds in dead. count_gap_size and count_gap_location set where the counts disagree. For replicate_sum, one replicate's categories do not add to its sown figure. For summary_pct, test.recorded_germ_pct differs from germinated over sown across non-excluded replicates. For inventory_draw, sample.inventory_before minus inventory_after differs from sample.seeds_drawn. For sown_vs_drawn, total sown exceeds seeds_drawn. A trivial gap is 1 to 2 seeds or under 1 point; a large gap is over 10 seeds or 5 points. contamination_level appears as replicates[].contaminated counts. Mitigation shows as that replicate's excluded set to true, or as a test.agar_transfer_date earlier than the dead counts were scored. incubator_excursion appears as an entry in incubator.excursions whose times fall between test.sow_date and test.actual_end. Mitigation shows as a non-null maintenance_ticket with a duration under six hours, or as an excursion before sample.pretreatment_end. test_completion appears as test.cut_test_date set to null, or as test.actual_end earlier than test.scheduled_end. prior_decline_points is computed by the reviewer from the history entries. history_protocol_mismatch places a different protocol code in the newest history entry, so the reviewer must use the newest entry with a matching code. replicate_spread varies the per-replicate germination rates. boundary_placement sets values exactly at threshold edges. Decoys include: heavy contamination in an excluded replicate; excursions logged outside the test window; a high initial_germ_pct that is decades old; a storage temperature field that is always the standard -20; and a sample.prior_retest_count that is unrelated to validity. No field may state validity, cause, decline, viability status or recommended action. The only summary figure is recorded_germ_pct, which may itself be wrong. There are no free-text fields; all values are numbers, ISO dates, booleans, codes or null.

F235.role: Hydrometric data quality officer reviewing completed river level gauge maintenance visit records
F235.setting: A regional river monitoring service sends field technicians to telemetered river level gauging stations for routine and reactive maintenance. Each visit produces a structured record: station details, visit logistics, check readings taken against the fixed staff board before and after work, the task list and parts used, defects left open, and short free-text notes from the technician and the duty supervisor. The data quality officer reviews one visit record at a time to decide whether the visit can be signed off, how the stage data since the previous visit should be treated, how large the pre-visit error was, and how serious any remaining defect is. Flood warning relies on these gauges, so open faults and doubtful data matter, but many alarming entries have ordinary explanations recorded elsewhere in the record.

sensor_fault_cause.instructions: Recorded level drift stems from a sensor fault, not channel change.

visit_disposition.instructions: What should happen next with this maintenance visit record?

criteria.sign_off: Visit complete and verified; close the record with no follow-up.
criteria.sign_off_noted: Close the record but log a minor point for next routine visit.
criteria.hold: Keep the record open pending one missing confirmation or reading.
criteria.planned_revisit: Book a routine return visit to finish outstanding work.
criteria.urgent_revisit: Dispatch a crew within days to fix a live measurement fault.

data_treatment.instructions: How should the stage data since the last visit be treated?

criteria.keep_as_recorded: Logged values stand unchanged because checks show them within tolerance.
criteria.apply_correction: Shift logged values by a verified offset with known start point.
criteria.mark_provisional: Keep values but flag them as unverified until cause confirmed.
criteria.reject_period: Withdraw logged values for the affected period as unusable.

offset_size.instructions: How large was the pre-visit logger offset against the staff board?
criteria: Negligible: offset under 5 mm between logger and board
Minor: offset from 5 mm to under 15 mm
Significant: offset from 15 mm to under 40 mm
Gross: offset of 40 mm or more

residual_defect.instructions: How severe is the worst defect left unresolved at the station?
criteria: No unresolved defect listed after the visit
Cosmetic or housing defect only, readings unaffected
Secondary channel degraded, primary stage sensor working
Primary stage sensor faulty but still reporting values
Primary stage sensor not reporting any values

factors.name: pre_visit_offset_mm
factors.description: True absolute difference between logger stage and staff board reading on arrival, before any adjustment; clustered near the 5, 15 and 40 mm boundaries in a share of records.

factors.name: check_reading_spread_mm
factors.description: Disagreement between the two staff board readings taken on arrival (wave action, surge); a large spread near a boundary leaves the offset level contested.

factors.name: drift_cause
factors.description: Actual cause of any drift: pressure transducer fault, channel change (gravel deposition, scour, weed growth), disturbed staff board datum, or no real drift.

factors.name: cause_evidence
factors.description: How well the record supports the drift cause: nothing beyond the offset, one indicator (e.g. sensor swapped and new one agrees), or corroborated by two independent checks (bench test plus level survey).

factors.name: visit_completion
factors.description: Share of planned tasks done: all, some (work started but unfinished), or visit aborted on site (high flow, access refused, unsafe bank).

factors.name: post_visit_check_logged
factors.description: Whether a staff board check after the work was recorded; when absent the visit cannot be verified and typically needs a hold.

factors.name: residual_defect_class
factors.description: Worst defect still open at departure: none, cosmetic (kiosk door, signage), secondary channel (rain gauge, water temperature), primary stage sensor faulty but reporting, primary stage sensor offline.

factors.name: backup_sensor_ok
factors.description: Whether an independent backup stage sensor (radar or shaft encoder) is installed and reporting normally; lowers urgency of primary faults without changing their severity.

factors.name: benign_explanation
factors.description: Presence of a recorded ordinary reason for an alarming signal: approved temporary offset from the hydrometry lead, recent weed cut, known flood debris event, planned works window on the reach.

factors.name: record_gap
factors.description: Which part of the record is missing or out of order: nothing, post-visit checks null, defects list absent, parts list null although a sensor swap is claimed, or supervisor sign-off dated before the visit.

factors.name: logger_gap_hours
factors.description: Hours of missing logger data during or around the visit; short gaps are normal during swaps, long gaps bear on data treatment.

factors.name: telemetry_decoy
factors.description: Battery voltage and signal strength values that sometimes look poor but have no bearing on stage accuracy unless the primary sensor is offline.

factors.name: note_tone
factors.description: Tone of the technician's free-text note, independent of the true state: alarming, neutral or reassuring; sometimes names a cause the evidence does not support.

sections.name: station
sections.description: Station id, river, gauge type, backup sensor fields, telemetry battery and signal values.

sections.name: visit
sections.description: Visit id, type, dates, crew, planned task count, arrival and departure times, abort reason.

sections.name: checks
sections.description: Pre and post visit staff board and logger stage readings with timestamps.

sections.name: works
sections.description: Task list with status per task, parts fitted with serials, bench test results.

sections.name: defects
sections.description: List of defects open at departure with channel affected and reporting state.

sections.name: notes
sections.description: Short free text: technician note, supervisor comment, sign-off date.

F235.rendering_notes: station: {station_id, river, gauge_type, backup: {type, installed, last_value_m, status}, telemetry: {batt_v, rssi_dbm, last_tx}}. backup_sensor_ok drives backup.installed and status ('reporting'/'stale'/null). telemetry_decoy sets batt_v (e.g. 11.4 vs 12.8) and rssi_dbm; these are decoys. visit: {visit_id, type ('routine'/'reactive'), planned_date, visit_date, arrive, depart, tasks_planned, abort_reason or null}; visit_completion shows only through works.tasks statuses and abort_reason, never as a summary field. checks: {pre: {board_m: [r1, r2], logger_m, time}, post: {board_m, logger_m, time} or null}; pre_visit_offset_mm is never stated, the reviewer must subtract logger_m from the mean of board_m (metres to 3 decimals); check_reading_spread_mm is the gap between r1 and r2. post is null when post_visit_check_logged is false or record_gap is post_checks_null. works: {tasks: [{task, status ('done'/'part_done'/'not_started')}], parts: [{part, serial_out, serial_in}] or null, bench_test: {result_mm_error, date} or null, logger_gap_h}. drift_cause and cause_evidence surface indirectly: sensor fault via a swapped transducer whose bench_test shows error matching the offset and post check agreeing; channel change via a task like 'control survey' with noted bed level change and a sensor bench test within spec; datum disturbance via 'board relevelled' task with survey difference; single_indicator records show only one of these, none shows none. defects: [{item, channel ('primary_stage'/'secondary'/'housing'), reporting (true/false), raised}] or absent when record_gap is defects_missing; residual_defect_class maps to the worst entry. notes: {tech_note, supervisor_comment, signed_off} where tech_note and supervisor_comment are one sentence each; note_tone sets wording of tech_note and may assert a cause ('gravel bar has built up again') that the readings do not confirm; benign_explanation appears as a supervisor_comment such as an approved temporary offset reference, a recent weed cut or a works window, about half the time alongside alarming signals. signoff_before_visit puts signed_off earlier than visit_date. No field may state the disposition, the data treatment, the offset band, a defect severity rating or the confirmed drift cause; no 'risk', 'priority' or 'status: ok' summaries beyond per-task and per-defect states a real field system would hold.

F236.role: Site technical QA officer at a contract bakery, reviewing each allergen changeover record before releasing the line and its first batch
F236.setting: A multi-line contract bakery runs products with different allergen profiles (wheat, egg, milk, sesame, tree nuts, soya) on shared mixers, depositors and ovens. Every changeover between products generates a structured record covering the transition, the cleaning steps, swab verification, the first production run, approvals and recent line history. The QA officer reads one record at a time and decides on release, the most serious deficiency, product exposure and residual allergen evidence.

swabs_cleared.instructions: Every required swab passed before the new run's first production.

criteria.true: All required swabs passed, including retests, before production start
criteria.false: Any swab failed, missing, or timed after start

line_disposition.instructions: What should happen to the line and first batch now?

criteria.release: Line and batch released with no further action required
criteria.release_conditional: Released with an added control, such as precautionary label or test
criteria.hold: Batch held until one missing confirmation is supplied
criteria.reclean_quarantine: Line recleaned and exposed product quarantined for disposal review

worst_deficiency.instructions: What is the most serious deficiency type in this record?

criteria.none: No deficiency found in cleaning, checks, sequence or records
criteria.records_only: Worst issue is paperwork: missing fields or mismatched identifiers
criteria.cleaning_shortfall: Worst issue is skipped clean steps or swabs over limit
criteria.release_breach: Production started before swabs passed or QA sign-off given

exposed_product.instructions: How much product was made before the line was verified clean?
criteria: No product made before verified clean
Under 50 kg made before verified clean
50 to 500 kg made before verified clean
Over 500 kg made before verified clean

residue_evidence.instructions: How strong is the evidence of residual allergen on the line?
criteria: Clear: all allergen swabs negative, no retests needed
Trace: a reading above zero but below limit
Cleared: reading at or over limit, retest passed
Persistent: reading over limit, retest failed or missing

factors.name: allergen_transition
factors.description: Direction of allergen change between outgoing and incoming product; removing an allergen from the next product is the high-risk case, same set is lowest

factors.name: cleaning_completion
factors.description: How fully the specified wet-clean procedure was carried out, shown by step completion flags and actual versus specified duration

factors.name: swab_outcome
factors.description: Allergen-specific swab results relative to action limit, including whether a retest was taken and passed

factors.name: swab_timing_mismatch
factors.description: A swab or retest timestamp in verification falls after the first batch start time in production, so it did not clear the line in time

factors.name: cross_section_discrepancy
factors.description: An unannounced mismatch between corresponding values in different sections; some records have none

factors.name: exposed_quantity_kg
factors.description: Kilograms of incoming product made between production start and the time the line was verified clean (all kilograms made if never verified)

factors.name: approved_deviation
factors.description: A QA-approved deviation covering the shortfall exists, such as an authorised alternative clean or a pre-agreed hold-and-test release

factors.name: label_precaution
factors.description: Incoming product's packaging already carries a precautionary statement covering the outgoing allergen, lowering consumer risk without curing the process gap

factors.name: dedicated_tooling
factors.description: Removable contact parts were swapped for an allergen-dedicated set rather than cleaned in place, reducing the effect of skipped steps

factors.name: qa_signoff_state
factors.description: Whether and when QA signed off line release relative to production start

factors.name: line_failure_history
factors.description: Count of failed allergen verifications on this line in its last ten changeovers

factors.name: boundary_value
factors.description: A key value sits exactly on a scale boundary: a swab reading equal to the action limit, or exposed quantity exactly 50 or 500 kg

sections.name: changeover
sections.description: Line ID, outgoing and incoming product codes, allergen lists for each, start and end timestamps

sections.name: cleaning
sections.description: List of procedure steps with completed flags, specified and actual minutes, chemical used, part swap flag, operator ID

sections.name: verification
sections.description: List of swabs: location, allergen target, method, reading, action limit, unit, timestamp, retest_of reference; plus ATP readings

sections.name: production
sections.description: Line ID, product code, first batch ID, start timestamp, quantity with unit, packaging allergen statement list, held flag

sections.name: approvals
sections.description: QA sign-off object with signer ID and timestamp or null; list of deviations with ID, scope and approval timestamp

sections.name: history
sections.description: Last ten changeovers on the line: date, outgoing and incoming codes, verification passed boolean

F236.rendering_notes: allergen_transition: shown only by comparing changeover.from_allergens and changeover.to_allergens lists; never labelled. cleaning_completion: cleaning.steps[].completed false for skipped steps, or actual_min below spec_min. swab_outcome: verification.swabs[] readings against limit_ppm per swab; retests appear as extra entries with retest_of pointing to the original swab ID; a missing retest is simply absent. swab_timing_mismatch: a swab timestamp later than production.start_at. cross_section_discrepancy: e.g. production.line_id differs from changeover.line_id, production.product_code differs from changeover.to_code, production.packaging_allergens omits an allergen in changeover.to_allergens, quantity unit g where kg expected, or a history entry's codes not matching. exposed_quantity_kg: derived by the reader from production.quantity and the gap between start_at and the last passing swab time; quantity is the batch total plus batch start/end times, never a pre-computed exposure figure. approved_deviation: approvals.deviations[] entry whose scope references the step or swab concerned, approved before start; decoy deviations reference other lines or expired dates. label_precaution: production.packaging_allergens includes a may_contain entry for the outgoing allergen. dedicated_tooling: cleaning.part_swap true with a dedicated set ID. qa_signoff_state: approvals.qa_signoff.signed_at before or after production.start_at, or null. line_failure_history: count of false in history[].verification_passed. boundary_value: reading equals limit_ppm exactly, or quantity lands on 50 or 500 kg. Decoys: ATP readings in RLU (general hygiene, not allergen-specific) sometimes high when allergen swabs are clean and low when allergen swabs fail; operator IDs; chemical batch numbers; ambient temperature; history entries on unrelated product pairs. The record never contains fields such as risk, disposition, release_decision, deficiency, exposed_kg or swab_status summaries; device result strings may appear per swab only as raw readings with limits. No free-text notes or comments appear anywhere.

F237.role: Notification desk reviewer at a self-certification scheme for registered electrical contractors
F237.setting: Registered contractors upload electrical installation certificates for completed domestic work. Before the scheme lodges each job with the local building control body, a reviewer checks one certificate record at a time. They confirm that the schedule of test results, the board details, the instruments and the signatory's registration all belong together. They also check that testing happened in the right order and that every circuit was tested. The reviewer then decides whether to lodge, lodge with advice, hold for a query, or return the certificate for retest.

results_match_install.instructions: Test results correspond to the installation described on this certificate.

criteria.true: Board, circuits and devices agree across every section
criteria.false: Circuit count, device ratings or board reference conflict

tested_before_signing.instructions: All testing was completed on or before the certificate signature date.

submission_disposition.instructions: What should the scheme do with this certificate submission?

criteria.lodge: Notify building control now; no contractor contact needed
criteria.lodge_with_advice: Notify now, and tell contractor about clerical errors only
criteria.hold_query: Withhold notification until contractor supplies one missing confirmation
criteria.return_retest: Reject certificate; installation must be retested and recertified

untested_circuits.instructions: How many scheduled circuits lack a complete set of test results?
criteria: None: every scheduled circuit has a full result set
One: exactly one circuit is missing a required result
Few: two or three circuits are missing results
Many: four or more circuits, or schedule absent

failed_checks.instructions: How many of the standard checks on this record failed?
criteria: No standard checks failed
Exactly one standard check failed
Two or three standard checks failed
Four or more standard checks failed

factors.name: install_type
factors.description: Kind of work certified; changes how many circuits and which tests are expected

factors.name: board_ways_declared
factors.description: Number of circuits declared on the board summary in supply_and_board

factors.name: schedule_mismatch
factors.description: Whether and where the circuit schedule disagrees with the board summary or job description

factors.name: incomplete_circuits
factors.description: Count of scheduled circuits with one or more required readings null

factors.name: worst_zs_ratio
factors.description: Worst measured earth loop impedance divided by the maximum permitted for its device

factors.name: test_date_order
factors.description: How circuit test dates relate to the job signature and completion dates

factors.name: rcd_test_status
factors.description: State of RCD trip-time results on circuits needing additional protection

factors.name: signatory_registration
factors.description: Signatory's scheme registration against the test date and work scope

factors.name: instrument_calibration
factors.description: Calibration due date of the listed test instrument relative to the test date

factors.name: retest_logged
factors.description: A remedial retest entry exists with a passing value for a failed or missing reading

factors.name: clerical_errors
factors.description: Count of harmless slips such as postcode format, client name spelling or swapped circuit descriptions

factors.name: days_to_upload
factors.description: Days between completion date and upload; a decoy that rarely changes the disposition

sections.name: job
sections.description: Certificate reference, site address, install_type, completion_date, signed_date, upload_date, signatory_reg_no

sections.name: contractor
sections.description: Registration record: reg_no, status, scope_codes list, valid_from, valid_to

sections.name: supply_and_board
sections.description: Earthing system, ze_ohm, pfc_ka, board_ref, ways_used, main_switch_a, rcd devices list

sections.name: circuits
sections.description: List of circuits: no, board_ref, ocpd_type, ocpd_a, csa_mm2, zs_max_ohm, zs_ohm, ir_mohm, rcd_ms, tested_on

sections.name: instruments
sections.description: List of test instruments: serial, kind, cal_due date

sections.name: remedial_retests
sections.description: List of retest entries: circuit_no, reading, value, retested_on; null when none

F237.rendering_notes: There are no free-text fields; every signal is a value, date or null. board_ways_declared appears as supply_and_board.ways_used. schedule_mismatch shows as the circuits list length differing from ways_used, one ocpd_a value differing from the matching rcd devices entry or board summary, or circuits[].board_ref differing from supply_and_board.board_ref. incomplete_circuits shows as nulls in zs_ohm, ir_mohm or rcd_ms; schedule_null sets circuits to null. worst_zs_ratio is never computed; the reviewer must compare zs_ohm with zs_max_ohm per row, and values near 1.0 are left for judgment. test_date_order is shown only through circuits[].tested_on compared with job.signed_date and completion_date, or as a null tested_on. rcd_test_status appears as rcd_ms values above 40, nulls, or an empty rcd devices list on circuits that need one. signatory_registration requires comparing job.signatory_reg_no and the test dates with contractor.reg_no, status, scope_codes and valid_to. instrument_calibration requires comparing instruments[].cal_due with tested_on, or finding a serial missing. retest_logged fills remedial_retests with a passing value dated after the original; it is null otherwise, with about half of the alarming readings mitigated this way. Decoys: clerical_errors (postcode spacing, name spelling, swapped circuit labels), days_to_upload, csa_mm2 and pfc_ka values that look unusual but are acceptable. Never include an overall pass/fail field, an outcome or recommendation field, a count of missing results, or any flag stating a mismatch or a late date.

F238.domain: sports pitch condition inspections before matches
F238.setting: A regional grassroots and semi-professional league requires every home club to log a pre-match pitch inspection record, combining the groundstaff's own report with the appointed inspector's independent zone readings, a hazard list, a remediation log and the short-range forecast. The inspector reviews one record at a time before kick-off and decides whether the fixture is playable and what happens next.

playable_as_is.instructions: The pitch is playable at kick-off without any further remedial work.

readings_agree.instructions: Groundstaff readings agree with the inspector's own measurements within tolerance.

criteria.true: Every shared measurement matches within its stated tolerance
criteria.false: At least one shared measurement differs beyond tolerance

fixture_decision.instructions: What should happen to the fixture after this inspection?

criteria.proceed: No open defects; match goes ahead on the main pitch.
criteria.proceed_conditions: Goes ahead on main pitch once named fixes or coning completed.
criteria.reinspect: Decision deferred to a timed second inspection before kick-off.
criteria.switch_pitch: Main pitch unfit; fixture moves to the certified alternate pitch.
criteria.postpone: Main pitch unfit and no alternate; fixture is postponed.

failing_zones.instructions: How many inspected pitch zones fail at least one surface check?
criteria: No inspected zone fails any surface check
Exactly one inspected zone fails a check
Two or three inspected zones fail checks
Four or more inspected zones fail checks

hazard_severity.instructions: How serious is the worst player-safety hazard recorded on the pitch?
criteria: None: no hazard recorded on the playing surface
Cosmetic: affects appearance only, not footing or ball
Minor: alters ball roll or footing, no injury mechanism
Significant: could cause slips or twists if left unmarked
Critical: hole, hard object or frozen ground risking injury

factors.name: sport
factors.description: Sport and code being played, which sets the zone layout and threshold table (grass height, firmness band, line widths).

factors.name: reading_mismatch
factors.description: Size of the gap between a groundstaff-reported value and the inspector's independent reading of the same quantity.

factors.name: mismatch_field
factors.description: Which shared quantity carries the mismatch, so discrepancies sit in varied places.

factors.name: worst_hazard
factors.description: Category of the most serious hazard among the listed items, expressed through hazard type codes rather than a severity label.

factors.name: failing_zone_count
factors.description: Number of inspected zones whose inspector readings breach at least one threshold for the sport.

factors.name: hazard_mitigated
factors.description: Whether the most alarming hazard is accompanied by mitigation: remediation logged and verified, area outside the playing lines, approved league exception, or a benign cause such as sprinkler residue already draining.

factors.name: remediation_status
factors.description: State of work on open defects as shown by the remediation log.

factors.name: weather_trend
factors.description: Forecast direction between inspection and kick-off: drying or thawing, stable, or worsening rain or frost.

factors.name: alternate_pitch_available
factors.description: Whether the venue has a certified alternate pitch free at kick-off time.

factors.name: hours_to_kickoff
factors.description: Time between the inspection timestamp and scheduled kick-off, deciding whether a reinspection or fix is feasible.

factors.name: note_contradiction
factors.description: Whether a free-text note contradicts the structured data, e.g. claims a zone cleared while the hazard list shows it open, or mentions a defect missing from the list.

factors.name: boundary_reading
factors.description: Whether a deciding reading sits exactly on its threshold or the tolerance edge, leaving judges split.

factors.name: prior_postponements
factors.description: Postponements at this venue earlier in the season; context and decoy that should not alone drive the decision.

sections.name: fixture
sections.description: Fixture id, sport, competition, venue id, pitch id, kick-off datetime, alternate pitch details and season postponement count.

sections.name: groundstaff_report
sections.description: Club groundstaff's own summary readings, report time and a one-sentence comment.

sections.name: inspector_readings
sections.description: Inspector's timestamped readings per zone with thresholds and tolerances, plus a short free-text note.

sections.name: hazards
sections.description: List of logged hazards with zone, type code, size, inside_playing_lines flag and exception reference.

sections.name: remediation_log
sections.description: List of remediation actions with zone, action code, started, completed and verified_by fields.

sections.name: forecast
sections.description: Hourly forecast to kick-off: rain_mm, air_temp_c, ground_frost flag and source.

F238.rendering_notes: fixture: sport, kickoff (ISO datetime), alt_pitch {id, certified bool, free bool} or null when none; alternate_pitch_available shows only as alt_pitch certified and free both true. prior_postponements as season_ppd integer (decoy). groundstaff_report: gmax, grass_mm, standing_water_pct, surface_temp_c, crossbar_mm, line_mm, reported_at, comment (one sentence). inspector_readings: inspected_at (hours_to_kickoff derived from this against fixture.kickoff, never stated), zones list of 6-9 entries {zone, gmax, grass_mm, standing_water_pct, surface_temp_c}, goals {crossbar_mm}, lines {width_mm}, thresholds object per sport with tolerance values, note (one sentence). reading_mismatch and mismatch_field appear only by comparing groundstaff values with the inspector's average or worst zone value of the same quantity; within_tolerance gaps are decoys. failing_zone_count is never stated; it must be counted by checking each zone against thresholds; boundary_reading places one value exactly on a threshold or tolerance edge. hazards: worst_hazard expressed through type codes (e.g. divot_scar, uneven_seam, surface_hole, glass_found, frozen_patch, worn_goalmouth) and size_cm; some hazards sit outside the playing lines (inside_lines false) as low-impact decoys. hazard_mitigated shows as exception_ref non-null, a matching remediation entry with verified_by, inside_lines false, or a forecast drying trend explaining standing water; it applies to the most alarming hazard about half the time. remediation_log: remediation_status shown by started/completed timestamps and verified_by null or initials; empty list when not_needed; in_progress has completed null. weather_trend appears only as hourly rain_mm and air_temp_c values and ground_frost flags, never a trend label. note_contradiction places a conflicting claim in inspector_readings.note or groundstaff_report.comment (e.g. 'goalmouth relaid and firm' while the hazard list keeps worn_goalmouth open). Unknown readings use null. No field ever states playable, decision, severity, failing count, agreement or risk.

F239.role: Digitisation quality assurance officer at a county record office, reviewing one captured archival item at a time before images are released to the online catalogue
F239.setting: A record office digitisation studio photographs bound volumes, loose papers, maps, photographic prints and parchment rolls. Each captured item produces a QC record that brings together catalogue metadata, capture session details, automated image metrics, the conservation condition report, prior rework history and delivery packaging status. The officer reviews each record and decides whether the image set is complete and sound, whether flagged faults belong to the original document or to the capture, what happens to the item next, and how much of it must be rescanned.

pages_complete.instructions: Every catalogued page of the item is present in the captured images.

criteria.true: Counts match, or each gap is a documented lacuna
criteria.false: Unexplained shortfall, or page count not yet verified

defects_original.instructions: Flagged image defects arise from the original document, not from capture.

criteria.true: Every flagged page has a matching condition entry
criteria.false: Any flagged page lacks a condition entry, or none flagged

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this captured item next?

criteria.accept: All checks complete and passed; release images to the catalogue
criteria.accept_conditional: Checks complete, only minor non-blocking faults; release and log fixes
criteria.hold: One check or confirmation still outstanding; pause release until it arrives
criteria.recapture: Confirmed capture fault blocks release; return item to the studio

recurrence_count.instructions: How often has this same issue been logged in 12 months?
criteria: First occurrence; not logged in prior 12 months
Logged once before within the past 12 months
Logged two to four times in 12 months
Logged five or more times in 12 months

recapture_share.instructions: What share of the item's images needs recapturing?
criteria: No images need recapturing
Fewer than 5% of images need recapturing
Between 5% and 25% of images
More than 25% of images need recapturing

factors.name: item_format
factors.description: Physical format of the archival item, which changes typical page counts, defect types and handling constraints

factors.name: page_count_gap
factors.description: Catalogued page or leaf count minus the number of captured images (0 means counts agree)

factors.name: gap_documented
factors.description: Whether the conservation report lists missing or excised leaves that account for the shortfall

factors.name: page_count_verified
factors.description: Whether a physical foliation check has been recorded; when false the captured-count comparison is null

factors.name: defect_image_share
factors.description: Share of captured images flagged by automated checks for blur, skew, glare, cropping or gutter shadow

factors.name: defects_match_condition
factors.description: Whether the flagged image numbers coincide with pages the conservation report records as foxed, torn, cockled or tightly bound

factors.name: colour_target_status

factors.name: recalibrated_after

factors.name: checksum_state

factors.name: qc_signoff_before_capture_end

factors.name: prior_rework_count

factors.name: boundary_case

F239.rendering_notes: item.leaf_count_catalogued against qc_metrics.images_captured carries page_count_gap indirectly; qc_metrics.foliation_check is an object {done: bool, checked_on: date or null}, and when page_count_verified is false it is {done:false, checked_on:null} with qc_metrics.images_expected set to null. gap_documented appears as conservation.lacunae, a list of {leaf_ref, kind: excised|missing|blank_unfoliated}; its length matches the gap when true, is empty or unrelated when false, and covers only part of the gap when boundary_case applies. defect_image_share is rendered as qc_metrics.flags, a list of {image_no, code: blur|skew|glare|crop|gutter}, whose length relative to images_captured gives the share; never state the percentage. defects_match_condition shows as conservation.entries [{leaf_ref, condition: foxing|tear|cockle|tight_binding|fading}] whose leaf refs either align with flagged image numbers (via item.image_leaf_offset) or do not. colour_target_status appears in capture.targets as a list of {taken_at, delta_e, limit}; not_captured gives an empty list; recalibrated_after adds capture.recalibrations [{at}] and a second passing target taken later. checksum_state is delivery.fixity {algorithm, state, checked_at or null}. qc_signoff_before_capture_end appears only as qc_metrics.signed_off_at earlier than capture.ended_at. prior_rework_count is the length of rework_history.events; it informs the separate recurrence scale and is a decoy for the current disposition. Decoys: capture.operator_grade (senior or trainee, unrelated to outcomes), capture.ppi above 400 for most records (only below-400 values matter for the format), item.access_restriction, delivery.release_target_date close by (urgency does not change the correct answer). No field may state the disposition, recapture share, completeness or defect origin; no summary fields such as status: fail or qc_result: ok beyond per-check values a real studio system would log. No free-text fields.

F240.role: Remote performance engineer at a solar O&M control centre, reviewing one inverter fault event record at a time
F240.setting: A utility-scale solar portfolio's monitoring platform raises a fault event record whenever a string or central inverter trips, derates or stops reporting. Each record bundles the asset register entry, the inverter's alarm log extract, SCADA telemetry for the event window, site context (grid, weather and maintenance schedules) and recent fault and repair history. The engineer checks whether the fault is a real inverter defect, whether it recurred after repair, how much yield was lost, how much capacity is still unavailable, and what to do next.

genuine_defect.instructions: Logged fault reflects a genuine inverter defect, not an external cause.

criteria.true: Evidence points to inverter hardware after grid and sensor checks.
criteria.false: External cause, sensor artefact, or too little evidence of a defect.

post_repair_repeat.instructions: Same fault has recurred on this inverter since its last completed repair.

criteria.true: Matching fault code logged after the repair completion date.
criteria.false: No repeat after repair, or no completed repair on record.

next_step.instructions: What next step should the engineer take for this fault?

criteria.close_log: Fault cleared with external or benign cause; no follow-up needed.
criteria.watch_list: Fault cleared but cause unclear; recheck at next daily review.
criteria.hold_confirm: One missing confirmation is needed before any further action is chosen.
criteria.scheduled_visit: Defect likely but output tolerable; add to the planned site visit.
criteria.urgent_dispatch: Defect likely with major output loss or safety risk; dispatch now.

yield_loss.instructions: What share of expected daily yield was lost to the fault?
criteria: Negligible: under 1% of expected daily yield lost
Minor: 1% to under 5% of expected yield lost
Material: 5% to under 20% of expected yield lost
Severe: 20% or more of expected yield lost

capacity_unavailable.instructions: How much rated capacity remains unavailable when the log closes?
criteria: Back at full rated output, no active limit
Derated, output limit at 50% to under 100%
Derated below 50% of rated but still exporting
Offline, exporting nothing at log close

factors.name: fault_class
factors.description: Underlying fault type recorded by the inverter firmware; sets which other signals matter (e.g. grid overvoltage is often external, insulation and IGBT faults usually hardware).

factors.name: log_telemetry_mismatch
factors.description: Size of disagreement between fault start/clear times in the alarm log and the zero/low-output window visible in telemetry; drives whether the logged duration or the telemetry should be trusted for loss.

factors.name: grid_event_concurrent
factors.description: Whether the substation event list shows a grid voltage or frequency excursion overlapping the fault start; mitigates a defect reading.

factors.name: maintenance_window_active
factors.description: Whether a planned maintenance or isolation window covers the inverter during the fault; explains trips and zero output benignly.

factors.name: neighbour_cross_check
factors.description: Whether neighbouring inverters on the same feeder showed the same dip, did not, or have no data; agreement points to an external cause or sensor issue.

factors.name: repeat_count_30d
factors.description: Number of same-code faults on this inverter in the previous 30 days, listed in history; some fall before and some after the last repair.

factors.name: last_repair_status
factors.description: State of the most recent work order: none, completed and verified by a retest, completed with no retest logged, or still open.

factors.name: current_limit_pct
factors.description: Active power limit at log close as a percentage of rated AC output; 0 means offline, 100 means no limit.

factors.name: yield_loss_pct
factors.description: True lost energy as a share of the inverter's expected daily yield, derived from expected minus actual kWh in the event window.

factors.name: low_irradiance_window
factors.description: Whether the fault occurred at dawn, dusk or under heavy cloud so plane-of-array irradiance was low; caps energy loss despite long duration.

factors.name: serial_mismatch
factors.description: Whether the inverter serial in the alarm log differs from the asset register, e.g. after an unregistered unit swap, making history attribution doubtful.

factors.name: boundary_placement
factors.description: Whether yield loss or current limit is placed exactly on a scale threshold (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%) or the repair completion time sits within minutes of a repeat fault.

sections.name: asset
sections.description: Asset register entry: inverter ID, serial, model, rated AC kW, block and feeder.

sections.name: fault_event
sections.description: Alarm log extract: serial, fault code, firmware severity code, start and clear timestamps, auto-restart attempts.

sections.name: telemetry
sections.description: SCADA samples for the window: AC kW, expected kW, irradiance, active limit, cumulative kWh.

sections.name: site_context
sections.description: Substation grid events, maintenance windows, neighbouring inverter output ratios for the window.

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of prior faults (date, code) in 30 days and recent work orders with status and retest flag.

F240.rendering_notes: asset: inverter_id, serial, model, rated_ac_kw, block, feeder. fault_event: serial (differs from asset.serial when serial_mismatch), code (from fault_class, e.g. 'F-ISO-02'), fw_severity (1-4, a real firmware field and a decoy: it is set independently of true impact), ts_start, ts_clear (null if not cleared), auto_restarts. telemetry: list of samples {ts, ac_kw, exp_kw, poa_wm2, limit_pct}, plus exp_day_kwh and act_window_kwh, exp_window_kwh; yield_loss_pct is never printed and must be computed as (exp_window_kwh - act_window_kwh)/exp_day_kwh; low_irradiance_window shows as low poa_wm2 values and small exp_kw. log_telemetry_mismatch shows as the zero-output stretch in samples starting or ending earlier/later than ts_start/ts_clear; for large mismatch the log duration would imply a very different loss. current_limit_pct appears only as the last sample's limit_pct and ac_kw versus asset.rated_ac_kw (offline shows ac_kw 0 and limit_pct 0). site_context: grid_events list {ts, type, magnitude_pu} overlapping ts_start when grid_event_concurrent, else unrelated or empty; maint_windows list {from, to, scope} covering the inverter ID when maintenance_window_active, with decoy windows for other blocks; neighbours list {inverter_id, output_ratio} with ratios below 0.8 when neighbours_affected, near 1.0 when normal, or null/empty when no data. history: faults list {date, code} with repeat_count_30d matching-code entries (others decoy codes), some dated before and some after the latest work order's completed date; work_orders list {wo_id, opened, completed (null if open), retest_ok (true/false/null)} reflecting last_repair_status. boundary_placement pushes computed loss or limit onto a threshold or puts a repeat fault minutes from completion. No field states defect verdict, recurrence, loss band, unavailability band or recommended action; no 'severity', 'risk', 'root_cause' or 'action' fields beyond fw_severity. Mitigations (grid event, maintenance window, affected neighbours, low irradiance) appear about equally with and without alarming signals; no free-text fields anywhere, all values numbers, ISO timestamps, booleans, codes or null.
